obituary.epitaph: When one key minted eighty million
obituary.obituary: On 22 March 2026, an attacker exploited Resolv's single-EOA minter: no oracle, no amount cap, no max-mint guard, depositing 100K USDC and receiving 50M USR in return, then iterating until 80M unbacked USR existed for ~$25M of extracted ETH. USR crashed to $0.025 in 17 minutes; the RLP insurance layer absorbed the bad debt and was wiped out, dragging Stream Finance's $17M position down with it. Resolv burned 46M of the unbacked supply via a blacklist freeze, but USR never recovered; by April it traded at $0.16 with $95M of collateral against $173M of liabilities. Delta-neutral collateral and Apostro-attested reserves were no defense against an operator-level privilege failure.

obituary.epitaph: Avalon closed its dollar and opened a claims desk
obituary.obituary: Avalon Labs discontinued USDa across every supported chain after concluding that bad actors had been extracting USDa liquidity through on-chain mechanisms. The October 3, 2026 notice told holders to submit a claim form and complete withdrawal by October 10 UTC, imposed a 5% monthly custodial fee on balances left unredeemed after that date, and asked contract, multisig and exchange-address holders to contact Avalon before claiming. The ordinary USDa-to-USDT conversion facility is closed. No observed market survives: the largest Ethereum USDa/USDT pool holds about $141K with zero 24-hour trades and quotes near $0.85, the other pools hold under $4K, CoinGecko lists no tickers, and about $145.6M was still recorded as circulating, almost unchanged over 30 days. Pharos freezes USDa as an archived discontinued asset; the issuer's recovery-claims desk is not a live redemption promise.
obituary.sourceLabel: Avalon Labs: Important Notice Regarding Recent Asset Adjustments

obituary.epitaph: Cabinet order ended the gold-backed dollar
obituary.obituary: USDKG announced on October 5, 2026 that issuance, circulation and blockchain operations would cease under Kyrgyz Cabinet Order 639-t dated August 20. The order directed liquidation of its issuer, EVA. Holders were directed to hello@usdkg.com to arrange fiat or USDT exchange, with no published payout duration. The issuer announced plans to consolidate and burn tokens and suspend the Ethereum and Tron contracts; completed burns and full holder repayment have not been established. Pharos preserves the token's historical market record as a frozen archive.

obituary.epitaph: Frax froze the CPI peg and wound down FPI
obituary.obituary: Frax launched FPI in March 2022 as an inflation-indexed unit of account whose redemption price tracked the U.S. CPI-U index through the FPI Controller Pool and FPIS governance token. Supply peaked near $114.0M before declining to roughly $7.0M by 2026. On June 17, 2026 Frax governance proposed FIP-448 to wind down the FPI system, and the Snapshot vote closed unanimously on June 28, 2026 (26.59M For, 0 Against). FIP-448 permanently froze FPI's CPI reference price, disabled new minting and LayerZero bridging, folded FPI's remaining balance sheet into Legacy FRAX, and left Ethereum redemptions into FRAX open.

obituary.epitaph: A Hyperliquid native made way for USDC
obituary.obituary: Native Markets and Bridge announced USDH's sunset in May 2026 as Hyperliquid markets migrated to USDC. New issuance ended except to support migration liquidity; the USDH dashboard was scheduled to close on July 17, while Bridge continued USDH-to-USDC and fiat redemption for onboarded holders. USDH remained fully backed during the transition, but its role as an active stablecoin product ended, so Pharos freezes it as an archived migration asset.

obituary.epitaph: A solvent euro was retired by its license boundary
obituary.obituary: Anchored Coins stopped issuing new AEUR after MiCAR made an EU issuer license necessary for the Swiss company to continue a EUR stablecoin business. The issuer moved reserves to Swissquote and kept a high-minimum redemption route for existing holders, but announced an orderly withdrawal from stablecoins rather than a relaunch. With issuance permanently closed and the product in a regulatory wind-down, Pharos freezes AEUR as an archived legacy asset while preserving its historical market record.

obituary.epitaph: Tether closed the gold-dollar experiment
obituary.obituary: Tether began winding down Alloy by Tether and aUSDt on June 17, 2026 after reviewing activity, demand, and product priorities. New positions and minting were closed, while existing users were given until September 17, 2026 to return aUSDt and recover XAUt collateral. The protocol remains available only to unwind existing exposure, so Pharos freezes it as an archived wind-down asset rather than an active issuance venue.
obituary.sourceLabel: Tether Alloy by Tether wind-down announcement

obituary.epitaph: Saved the protocol at the cost of its dollar
obituary.obituary: Launched in 2018, sUSD was Synthetix's flagship synthetic dollar, an overcollateralized stablecoin minted against staked SNX. Its peg held for years on a single reflex: whenever sUSD slipped below $1, stakers bought it back at a discount to repay their debt at par. SIP-420 (April 2025) dismantled that reflex, cutting the required collateral ratio from 750% to 200% and pooling debt collectively. Minting got cheap, but no individual was left with a reason to defend the dollar. sUSD fell to $0.68 within weeks and never recovered, drifting below peg for over a year as supply bled from a ~$329M peak toward a functionally insolvent tail near $0.23. In June 2026 Synthetix governance stopped repairing it and passed SIP-423: the contract was frozen, a holder snapshot taken, and sUSD made permanently non-transferable, with remaining holders entitled to 4 SNX per sUSD, locked for one year and then vested over a second year from the freeze. Unclaimed receipts expire worthless after six months. sUSD held in LP pools, vaults or other deposit contracts cannot be recovered directly; those holders go through a separate Treasury claims process using their deposit or LP receipt tokens, evaluated case by case.

obituary.epitaph: Noble's dollar entered maintenance mode
obituary.obituary: Noble moved USDN to maintenance mode on 2026-07-07 and said the USDC-USDN swaps pool on Noble would be closing soon. Holders may bridge USDN to Ethereum as wM and exchange wM for USDC on Uniswap.

obituary.epitaph: The magic ran out at nine cents
obituary.obituary: Once one of DeFi's largest CDP stablecoins, MIM peaked above $3.6B before repeated cauldron exploits and years of thinning liquidity hollowed out its market. The final break began on June 8, 2026. Abracadabra injected liquidity, offered SPELL incentives, raised rates across every cauldron, and suspended Curve bribes to force debt repayment, but none restored the peg. By July 26 MIM traded near $0.09 with roughly $3M circulating after seven weeks below peg, leaving no credible liquidity or arbitrage path back to one dollar.

obituary.epitaph: The chain that issued Blast's dollar switched itself off
obituary.obituary: Blast announced on October 2, 2026 that it would wind down its Ethereum L2 because operating costs exceeded revenue, and the normal withdrawal interface closed on October 26 with about $40.4M still sitting in the canonical bridge. USDB exists only on Blast: users receive it by bridging USDC, USDT or DAI to the L2, and redeem it for DAI only by proving a withdrawal back to Ethereum, so the end of the chain ends the product even though the L1 bridge contracts still accept contract-level exits. Supply fell from about $11.4M to $8.6M in the month to capture, every tracked Blast USDB pool shows zero 24-hour volume, and CoinGecko's last quote on October 30 came from those idle pools. Pharos freezes USDB as an archived wind-down asset; holders keep the L1 bridge claim described in Blast's withdrawal guides.

obituary.epitaph: Zoth retired its legacy dollar
obituary.obituary: Zoth's legacy V1 ZeUSD router is paused, and by 2026-10-31 the token was no longer listed on zoth.io or the Zoth app while its documentation page returned 404. Supply has stayed unchanged with no mints or burns, and the only pool held about $87 with no trading.
obituary.sourceLabel: Zoth product site (ZeUSD no longer listed)

obituary.epitaph: Immutable credit met mutable collateral
obituary.obituary: Nerite built USND on immutable Liquity V2-style contracts, but one of its approved collateral branches depended on rsETH. After the rsETH hack impaired that collateral, Nerite could not patch the market away or rewrite the risk controls. Supply collapsed from a $2.7M peak to under $100K, leaving USND as an archived case study in how immutable CDP systems can still inherit external collateral failure when a supported asset breaks upstream.

obituary.epitaph: A CDP stranded on a shuttered chain
obituary.obituary: Orki USDK was deployed only on Swellchain. Swellchain shut down its bridge flow in June 2026 and moved to halt chain operations on June 30, leaving remaining positions dependent on direct contract access or unrecoverable as the network wound down. Because USDK had no verified deployment outside Swellchain, Pharos freezes it as a discontinued single-chain CDP stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: Fixed-rate credit that never found its market
obituary.obituary: Ebisu offered fixed-rate, open-term credit through ebUSD, a Liquity v2 fork minting against weETH, sUSDe, WBTC, LBTC, and stcUSD branches natively on Ethereum and Plasma. Launched in June 2025, it never found scale: supply peaked near $815K and sat below $25K by July 2026. The team explored just-in-time liquidations, multichain issuance, structured looping and leverage vaults, and acquisition options, but could not grow ebUSD liquidity enough to support meaningful borrowing activity. On July 29, 2026 Ebisu announced it would wind down: minting was paused, users were asked to close Troves and withdraw Stability Pool deposits and DEX liquidity, and the frontend will be deprecated on October 30. An orderly, solvent sunset. Collateral redemption remained open throughout.

obituary.epitaph: Verification failed before the dollar did
obituary.obituary: Main Street's msUSD collapsed after Accountable terminated its verification relationship on June 20, 2026, saying the protocol failed verification standards. msUSD fell far below the dollar and remained around $0.29-$0.33 in the following week while independent on-chain analysts reported minimal immediately redeemable reserves against tens of millions of tokens. Main Street disputed the characterization and said assets remained backed, but the combination of failed third-party verification, unresolved redemption capacity, and persistent market pricing made msUSD unsuitable for active stablecoin tracking.

obituary.epitaph: The wrapper followed the parent down
obituary.obituary: msY is a strategy-vault wrapper over msUSD, so the June 2026 msUSD collapse impaired the wrapper's durable dollar backing. As msUSD depegged after Accountable terminated reserve verification, msY also traded far below its prior net-asset value and could not recover independently from the parent asset. Pharos freezes msY with msUSD as a derivative collapse rather than treating the vault share as an active stablecoin-like dollar instrument.
obituary.sourceLabel: Protos Main Street vault collapse report

name: Dinari USD+
launchPhaseDetail: Publicly issued; active tracking awaits the Safety Score new-asset evidence gate. Price and supply lanes pass, but 17 own open questions and the Mint Authority control inventory remain unresolved.

milestones.title: Dinari announces USD+ availability on Ethereum mainnet
milestones.description: Dinari's launch announcement states that USD+ and stUSD+ are available on Ethereum mainnet with a public minting and redemption app. This dates the instrument's public issuance, before the current replacement deployments; it does not establish the current token's control inventory.

obituary.epitaph: An orderly exit from Asia credit
obituary.obituary: Mu Digital announced an orderly wind-down of AZND, loAZND, and muBOND on July 10, 2026, and opened its redemption portal on August 7, 2026. Secondary trading had already collapsed: Pharos accepted its last admissible price, 0.19444 from the thin Curve pool, on July 20, 2026, and the residual pool now holds roughly $767 of liquidity near $0.03. CoinGecko stopped updating the feed on July 10 and DefiLlama delisted the project, leaving no admissible market or provider path. Pharos freezes AZND as an archived wind-down asset rather than an active stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: One compromised mint key broke the backing
obituary.obituary: StablR suspended USDR minting and redemption after a May 24, 2026 cybersecurity incident let an attacker mint unbacked USDR as part of a coordinated USDR/EURR exploit. StablR disclosed that the affected tokens were temporarily not backed 1:1 under MiCAR, announced on May 29 that its Board had activated its Recovery Plan, and on August 25 put unauthorised USDR in circulation at about 14.33M while stating that properly issued tokens remained fully backed. With no public restoration of minting, redemption, or full backing confirmed, Pharos freezes USDR as an archived incident asset rather than treating it as an active redeemable stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: Subsidized borrowing that ran out of runway
obituary.obituary: dTRINITY launched dUSD in December 2024 as the debt asset of its subsidized lending market, minting it 1:1 against whitelisted reserve stablecoins and supporting the peg with Curve AMO and buyback operations. On October 29, 2026 the team announced it would sunset the protocol, saying it needed more capital to keep building, including defences against AI-enabled security threats, and could not raise it in the current market. The protocol kept operating for an orderly wind-down: redemption fees fell to 10 bps, dLEND interest rebates, Curve rewards and the points program ended, AMO liquidity was to be phased out, and the planned TRIN token was cancelled. Holders exit by redeeming reserve assets or selling on Curve; borrowers must repay before lenders and stakers can fully withdraw. About 1.31M dUSD remained outstanding at capture.

obituary.epitaph: A savings vault that closed with its lending market
obituary.obituary: sdUSD was dTRINITY's staked dUSD receipt: deposits were supplied into dLEND and the share price accrued lending yield. It ended with its protocol. On October 29, 2026 dTRINITY announced it would sunset, discontinuing Curve rewards for the dUSD and sdUSD pools along with dLEND interest rebates. Holders can unstake only when dLEND has idle liquidity, which returns as dUSD borrowers repay; sharply higher borrowing rates while liquidity is low were meant to drive that deleveraging. About $317K of sdUSD remained outstanding at capture.

obituary.epitaph: Backed retired its first token line
obituary.obituary: Backed announced in March 2026 that it was consolidating onto xStocks and would gradually wind down the bToken line, including bIB01, by the end of 2026. New bIB01 issuance is closed and the issuer still supports redemption for existing holders.

obituary.epitaph: Pristine custody, wound down for want of demand
obituary.obituary: GYEN was GMO-Z.com Trust's NYDFS-chartered yen stablecoin, backed by FDIC-insured cash and short-dated U.S. Treasury bills, with monthly Network Firm attestations and one of the most tightly regulated issuer stacks of any JPY stablecoin. Its weakness was never custody but demand: thin secondary liquidity and a history of depegs (most infamously a squeeze above 1.5x peg in 2021 that triggered the Donovan v. Coinbase class action) left it trading more like a neglected FX derivative than a stablecoin. On May 15, 2026 GMO-Z.com Trust Company announced an orderly wind-down of GYEN and ZUSD, disabling purchases and opening a redemption-only window through November 11, 2026; parent GMO Internet Group moved to dissolve the U.S. subsidiary and recorded a ¥2.2bn write-down. With issuance ended and only redemption remaining, Pharos freezes GYEN as an archived wind-down asset rather than an active redeemable stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: A prepaid yen rail yielded to Japan's new stablecoin regime
obituary.obituary: JPYC Inc. permanently ended new issuance and exchange support for its prepaid JPYC series on June 1, 2025 as Japan's revised Payment Services Act took effect. Existing balances remain usable for the issuer's prepaid-payment services and transfers, but cannot be redeemed for cash and no longer have a primary issuance path. The separately tracked funds-transfer-token JPYC is the successor product; Pharos freezes v1 as its historical legacy series.
obituary.sourceLabel: JPYC Prepaid issuance and exchange termination notice

obituary.epitaph: Gold token wound up with its issuer
obituary.obituary: unbanked (TSE 8746) resolved on 2026-10-16 to abolish its crypto business and dissolve Kinka (BVI) Ltd., the XNK issuer, by 2027-03-31. The Ethereum buyback and bullion-exchange window closed at 2026-10-30 17:00 JST, and the issuer scheduled all recovered XNK plus the never-sold Cardano supply for burning in October 2026.

obituary.epitaph: Acquired, integrated, retired
obituary.obituary: Paxos completed its acquisition of Membrane Finance in February 2025 to absorb its Finnish EMI license and EU stablecoin issuance rails. As Paxos consolidated its product lineup, the EUROe business line was decommissioned and the platform transitioned to redemption-only mode in May 2026, with no new minting or trading. Existing holders were instructed to complete KYC and redeem outstanding EUROe 1:1 for euros via SEPA through Paxos Issuance Europe.

obituary.epitaph: A mint key broke the euro rail
obituary.obituary: StablR suspended EURR minting and redemption after a May 24, 2026 cybersecurity incident let an attacker mint 4.5M unbacked EURR as part of a coordinated EURR/USDR exploit. StablR disclosed that the affected tokens were temporarily not backed 1:1 under MiCAR while recovery work continued. With no public restoration of minting, redemption, or full backing confirmed, Pharos freezes EURR as an archived incident asset rather than treating it as an active redeemable stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: Overcollateralized on paper, unredeemable in practice
obituary.obituary: USX was dForce's CDP-style stablecoin, launched in 2021 and peaking above $205M in mid-2022. It never fully recovered the peg after the 2022 bear market: legacy debt positions on the dForce/Unitus lending protocol left circulating USX without a credible par-redemption route, and the discount widened from cents to a chasm. The terminal slide came in early 2026: below $0.75 in February, below $0.45 by April, and roughly $0.39 by July, with on-chain liquidity measured in tens of thousands of dollars and daily volume under $10. With the DF governance token near zero, no published remediation plan, and no redemption at par, Pharos froze USX as a collapsed archive asset.

obituary.epitaph: HomeCoin's mortgage dollar went dark
obituary.obituary: HomeCoin's issuer site returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-31 after its last archived capture on 2026-07-25, and its documentation repository has had no commits since 2022-12-16. Supply was unchanged at about 6.07M HOME and the two known pools held roughly $15K and $12K.

obituary.epitaph: Minted by facilitators, redeemable by no one
obituary.obituary: cdxUSD was Cod3x's GHO-style credit dollar on Base, where a 3-of-9 facilitator Safe held the only mint and burn keys and ordinary holders were never given a redemption route. The peg broke on August 27, 2026, when the hourly series first printed $0.8724 and both CoinGecko's daily close and the Aerodrome cdxUSD/WETH pool ended below $0.90; the price fell through $0.54 on August 28 and bottomed at $0.2457 on September 17. Supply never moved, holding at exactly 6,150,000 cdxUSD since January 2026 with the facilitator bucket level equal to total supply, so no token was burned at par during the collapse. Cod3x had already stopped supporting it: cod3x.org, its documentation index, and the technical article Pharos cites now describe only AI perp-trading agents, and that article returns 404. With roughly $23 of daily volume left across pools whose deepest executable side holds about $1,600, and DefiLlama flagging the project dead, Pharos freezes cdxUSD as an archived abandoned asset rather than an active stablecoin.
obituary.sourceLabel: CoinGecko Cod3x USD market data (below $0.90 since 2026-08-27)

obituary.epitaph: The only market went quiet
obituary.obituary: XT.com's official xtusd_usdt market stopped updating on July 18, 2026: the exchange ticker froze at that timestamp, the order book emptied, and the pair no longer appears in the exchange's symbol list. CoinGecko ended the feed on July 20 with an implausible tail near $0.04, and CoinMarketCap lists the asset inactive. XTUSD circulates on XSC, which Pharos does not index, so no contracts are configured and no identity-safe DEX route can be expressed. With the last admissible price at 0.93205 on July 20 and roughly $1.25M still circulating, Pharos freezes XTUSD as an archived market-ended asset rather than an active stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: The game-chain dollar stepped aside for bridged USDC
obituary.obituary: WEMIX transitioned its USD stablecoin activity from WEMIX$ to USDC.e, withdrawing Foundation liquidity from WEMIX$ pools and ending swap support across WEMIX.Fi and WEMIX PLAY in April 2026. Holders' WEMIX$ became eqWEMIX$, exchangeable 1:1 for USDC.e in the WEMIX$ Module; WEMIX$ can no longer be exchanged, and pool withdrawals run to 2027-03-05. Pharos freezes WEMIX$ as the retired native stablecoin while keeping its residual supply and history available in the archive.

obituary.epitaph: The Djed bank set a closing date with ADA still in the vault
obituary.obituary: COTI launched DJED on Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023 as a Djed reserve-bank stablecoin: holders minted and burned DJED against an ADA reserve, and the SHEN reserve coin absorbed ADA volatility inside a 400% to 800% reserve-ratio band. Supply peaked at about $6.0M in December 2023 and stood near $3.8M in January 2026 before falling through the year. Pharos's July and October 2026 reviews found the reserve ratio below the 400% minting floor, and the official dashboard showed 332% with zero mintable DJED on October 30, so holders could burn DJED but not mint it. On November 17, 2026 the Djed team announced that DJED and SHEN services will wind down at 23:59 UTC on December 31, 2026. It told holders to redeem through djed.xyz after withdrawing any liquidity-pool or lending positions, said every redemption is subject to the reserve ratio, and said remaining funds will be allocated to outstanding DJED and SHEN holders once the wind-down completes. At the November 19 archive capture about $984K of DJED was still in circulation, down from $1.42M a month earlier, and traded near $0.972, while the Djed bank contract held about 22.4M ADA (about $3.45M). Pharos freezes DJED as an archived wind-down asset; the protocol redemption window that closes on December 31 is the holder exit, not a continuing stablecoin.
obituary.sourceLabel: Djed: DJED and SHEN wind-down announcement

obituary.epitaph: Fathom shut down its CDP dollar; the residual token kept trading
obituary.obituary: Fathom's CDP-backed dollar entered shutdown on August 26, 2026, when its documented ShowStopper contract was caged in XDC transaction 0x07a63d9a4f3ad3859b6fff6d35fbe98074980d3bcac8b26f572532d82c67ffc9 at block 106506290. The shutdown disabled ordinary issuance and peg operations; the contract still reports live() = 0 with the same shutdown timestamp. This followed the issuer's recorded August wind-down announcement. FXD remained a residual traded token, with a sparse CoinGecko observation near $0.8423 at the November 8 archive capture. Pharos preserves its market history as a frozen wind-down asset rather than treating residual trading as an operating stablecoin.

obituary.epitaph: An 18-month beta retired behind its successor
obituary.obituary: Solomon Labs began an orderly wind-down of the original USDv and sUSDv system in preparation for the public launch of the new USDv. Legacy rewards ended and the final distribution occurred on August 27, 2026, the sUSDv unstaking-request deadline was October 9, 2026, and the legacy front end and support ended on October 16, 2026. The two tokens are separate with no automatic conversion: holders exit legacy USDv into USDC through the Meteora USDv/USDC pool, then acquire the new USDv. The basis positions are being closed and the legacy programs deprecated. About 1.51M USDv remained outstanding at capture; Pharos freezes the original mint as an archived legacy asset and continues to track the replacement mint separately.
obituary.sourceLabel: Solomon Labs: Winding Down the Original USDv

name: Fiserv USD
launchPhaseDetail: Platform live; Q1 2026 earnings (May 5): CEO Lyons confirms stablecoin pilot for interbank money movement; Huntington confirmed as pilot partner alongside Bank of North Dakota and others (cross-border, digital escrow); INDX cash settlement launched Feb 2026; StoneCastle acquired; May 14 Investor Day positioned FIUSD as a core strategic growth vector ('issued through banks, accepted through merchants'). At the Bernstein Strategic Decisions conference (June 3 2026) CEO Lyons confirmed 'FIUSD goes live in July,' setting July 2026 for the interbank platform launch. That window closed without a launch announcement. The Q2 2026 earnings release filed with the SEC on August 6 2026 does not mention FIUSD, stablecoins, digital assets, or Solana anywhere, and Fiserv cut its full-year guidance in the same release; the earnings call transcript is equally silent. Fiserv's digital asset platform went live on October 1 2026 hosting Roughrider Coin rather than FIUSD; on October 5 Fiserv said it had pivoted away from Paxos and Circle toward a more proprietary coin, joined the Open USD consortium, and gave no FIUSD launch date. Pharos cleared the remaining 2026 expectation on November 8 2026 after the October 5 interview gave no timetable.

The first live use case is Bank of North Dakota's Roughrider Coin, which VersaBank issues and custodies (minting, burning, custody and reserve asset management), with Fireblocks infrastructure and settlement on Solana. The release names no FIUSD launch.

milestones.description: Fiserv's head of embedded finance Sunil Sachdev told Payments Dive the company pivoted away from the Paxos and Circle partnership announced in June 2025 toward a more proprietary coin, and gave no FIUSD launch date. Fiserv joined the Open USD consortium in September 2026, plans to name wallet partners before year-end, and cited Bank of North Dakota's Roughrider Coin, live on its digital asset platform since October 1, as its first hosted stablecoin.

name: Qivalis Euro
launchPhaseDetail: 37-institution consortium across 15 countries (May 20 expansion added 25 new member banks to 12 existing members, including new arrivals ABN AMRO, Intesa Sanpaolo, Rabobank and Nordea; Raiffeisen Bank International was already a member); Fireblocks selected as core infrastructure partner Apr 21; French Finance Minister Lescure publicly endorses project (Apr 17); De Nederlandsche Bank granted Qivalis electronic money institution authorisation, announced October 14 2026; Qivalis says issuance will begin in the coming months once MiCA requirements are met and the token white paper is published; ERC-20F standard with built-in governance/AML/KYC; launching on Ethereum (primary), Polygon, Base with permissioned KYC layer. Qivalis has not itself published a ticker; Pharos uses EURqi, the name ESMA's interim MiCA register gives the white paper Qivalis notified on October 21 2026, and the register's qivalis.eu link to that document returned a 404 error on November 15 2026. No launch date accompanied the authorisation and the H2 2026 target stands; September 8 2026 secondary reports reaffirmed public Ethereum as the issuance chain without a Qivalis press release.

milestones.title: Five Spanish banks prepare to join Qivalis
milestones.description: Sabadell, Bankinter, Abanca, Kutxabank and Cecabank were preparing to join Qivalis; the report did not establish completed membership.

milestones.title: Consortium expands to 37 banks across 15 countries
milestones.description: Qivalis announced 25 new member banks, expanding the consortium from 12 to 37 institutions across 15 countries. New members include ABN AMRO, Intesa Sanpaolo, Rabobank and Nordea; Raiffeisen Bank International was already a member.

milestones.description: Third-party analysis and Qivalis's own site confirm the electronic-money-institution application has been formally submitted and is pending before De Nederlandsche Bank ('applied… not yet authorised'); the exact filing date is unpublished. milestones.description: Issuer confirmation, reported by Genfinity and echoed by Ethereum institutional ecosystem accounts, that the 37-bank consortium's token will be issued on public Ethereum using Fireblocks ERC-20F with built-in allowlist and denylist controls, with exchange and market-maker liquidity talks continuing pending the DNB licence.

milestones.title: Qivalis says it is close to securing the DNB EMI licence and targets go-live by end of 2026
milestones.description: CEO Jan-Oliver Sell told CoinDesk the company has grown to about 40 staff and is close to securing the Dutch electronic-money-institution licence, with the aim of going live with a regulated euro stablecoin by the end of the year. DNB authorisation remains the gate; the H2 2026 window is unchanged and no token has launched.

milestones.title: Qivalis appoints Olga Elsenga as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer
milestones.description: Qivalis appointed Olga Elsenga, formerly Head of Legal at ClearBank Europe and a management board member at Worldline's Global Collect Services, as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer effective October 1 2026. The company states it is still progressing towards DNB authorisation as an electronic money institution, is not yet authorised, and plans to launch before the end of 2026.

milestones.title: De Nederlandsche Bank authorises Qivalis as an electronic money institution
milestones.description: Qivalis announced that DNB granted it electronic money institution authorisation, making it eligible to issue euro electronic money tokens. Qivalis says issuance will begin in the coming months once MiCA requirements are met and the token white paper is published. No launch date or ticker was given.

milestones.title: ESMA records the EURqi white paper notification
milestones.description: ESMA's interim MiCA register lists a Qivalis B.V. white paper titled EURqi white paper, notified on October 21 2026 with DNB as competent authority. Notification is not white paper approval or evidence of circulation, and Qivalis had not published the document or a ticker by November 15 2026.

name: Polaris USDp
launchPhaseDetail: Public testnet open on Sepolia at testnet.polaris.finance (the earlier app.testnet.polarisfinance.io host no longer resolves); official documentation is live at docs.polaris.finance. Polaris has moved from polarisfinance.io to polaris.finance (currently a coming-soon page linking the testnet, docs, and @polarisfnd), took its earlier blog offline, and now brands the asset USDp rather than pUSD. On October 26 2026 Polaris said four audits were underway, without naming auditors, publishing reports or announcing a mainnet date. The former site stated no date was set and prioritised security over speed, so the earlier 2026-Q4 expectation was retired on 2026-08-05. A $1M angel round with Ethereum Foundation, Liquity, LI.FI, Altitude, and Fusion participation was reported on September 4 2026, without a mainnet date.

milestones.title: Polaris introduces self-scaling stablecoin operating system
milestones.description: Three-token model (pETH, pUSD, POLAR) with immutable code design and uncorrelated yield from protocol revenues; pUSD has since been renamed USDp.

milestones.title: Private testnet goes live
'Sustaining the Ecosystem: pETH & pUSD Flows' published
milestones.description: Documents Polaris's autonomous protocol-revenue distribution mechanism routing borrower interest and liquidation flows to USDp (then pUSD) Stability Pool participants by holdings.

milestones.title: TokenBrice publishes 'The Path to the North Star' founder narrative
milestones.description: Long-form post outlining Polaris's three-pillar mission (counterparty-free yield, ETH-correlated yield alternatives, restoring DeFi credibility) and tracing the protocol's lineage to Robert Lauko's bonding-curve research; mainnet timeline still uncommitted.

milestones.title: Polaris documentation renames pUSD to USDp
milestones.description: The official docs at docs.polaris.finance describe USDp as the native Polaris dollar (115% minimum collateral ratio, pETH collateral, Earn Vault), and the Sepolia testnet app at testnet.polaris.finance uses the USDp label throughout. The docs repository was created on June 8 2026 and its diagrams switched to USDp wording on June 22; the earlier Polaris blog posts used pUSD.

milestones.title: Polaris docs define an immutable core with bounded Stewardship
milestones.description: The Security Guarantees page states that the core protocol is immutable with no admin privileges, that USDp has no freeze or blacklist function, and that no privileged actor can mint outside the pETH-collateralized process. A bounded Stewardship role can still change interest rate splits, POLAR conversion parameters, flow recipients and weightings, and replace faulty oracle feeds; it cannot upgrade core contracts, add collateral, or change the bonding curve or liquidation mechanics. Stewardship decisions run through vePOLAR, the staked form of POLAR, which the docs renamed sPOLAR on October 14 2026. The docs do not say whether a timelock applies.

milestones.title: Polaris closes $1M angel round with Ethereum Foundation, Liquity, and LI.FI participation
milestones.description: Polaris reported a $1 million angel round joined by the Ethereum Foundation, Fusion (IPOR), Altitude, Liquity, LI.FI, and more than 30 founders and contributors including Anthony Sassano, to build pETH as yield-bearing collateral for USDp and GOLDp. No mainnet date accompanied the round, and the Polaris blog carried no post about it.

milestones.title: Polaris consolidates on polaris.finance; former domain now serves only a move notice
milestones.description: A polaris-docs commit repointed documentation at polaris.finance; polarisfinance.io now shows only the move notice and the retired blog survives solely in web.archive.org captures. The Sepolia testnet app remains labelled Alpha, docs state no production addresses, audit status, or launch status may be inferred from testnet values, and no mainnet date or audit announcement accompanied the consolidation.

milestones.title: Polaris docs rename the USDp Earn Vault to the Earn Pool
milestones.description: Commit 1c1b0b9 in the public polaris-docs repository replaced the Earn Vaults page with an Earn Pools page, now live at docs.polaris.finance/architecture/earn-pools. USDp deposited in the Earn Pool absorbs liquidations below the 115% minimum collateral ratio and earns a protocol-defined minimum share of minter interest, paid in USDp, plus pETH liquidation gains. As liquidations occur, a deposit's USDp balance falls while its pETH balance rises, so depositors take on ETH exposure. Deposits are transferable NFTs; auto-compounding vaults are third-party products outside the core protocol.

obituary.epitaph: The savings coin closed the vault
obituary.obituary: By April 2026, Buck's public site had become a shutdown notice saying the project was closed and funds were returned to token holders, while the former transparency page no longer served a reserve disclosure. Pharos freezes BUCK as a discontinued archive rather than an active yield-bearing stablecoin: the last live cache showed only about $4.6K of residual supply, no reliable price, and no working issuer reserve feed. The failure mode was an orderly wind-down rather than an oracle or collateral break, but live monitoring no longer has an active issuer disclosure surface to follow.

name: Revolut GBP Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Selected as one of four firms for FCA Regulatory Sandbox stablecoin cohort (Feb 25); testing began Q1 2026; full UK banking licence granted Mar 11, but GBP stablecoin would be issued from Revolut Ltd (e-money entity), not Revolut Bank UK, per BoE proposed rule on subsidiary issuance; Head of UK Policy Rory Tanner outlined proposition to House of Lords (Mar 25), flagging UK→India remittance corridor as priority use case; ticker not publicly confirmed; the Bank of England softened its stance in May 2026, dropping the £20k individual holding cap in favour of aggregate issuer caps (revised draft rules due June 2026) and signalling banks may issue branded coins via ring-fenced subsidiaries, though the 40% unremunerated-reserve requirement remains under review. On June 2 2026 the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee urged the BoE to scrap individual holding limits entirely and reconsider that 40% floor. On June 22 2026 the BoE published its final policy statement and draft rules: individual holding limits are scrapped in favour of a temporary per-coin issuance cap (initially ~£40bn / $50bn), the short-dated-UK-T-bill reserve share rises to 70% with the remainder held at the BoE and no yield paid to holders, and par redemption within 24 hours is required; a Code of Practice consultation runs to September 22 2026, with rules finalised by end-2026 and regulated sterling stablecoins operating from 2027. On August 26 2026 Revolut shipped the first token of its stablecoin programme: the euro-denominated EURR, on Ethereum, issued by Bridge Building S.A. (Stripe's Bridge) under MiCA rather than by a Revolut entity. That establishes Revolut's working issuance template as a third-party regulated issuer relationship, though it carries no direct read-through to sterling. The June 30 2026 BoE/FCA paper says firms wishing to issue stablecoins in the UK before October 25 2027 should be registered with the FCA, so the regime start is not a Revolut launch date. The June 30 2026 BoE/FCA joint approach sets the FCA regime start at October 25 2027, with systemic issuers transferring to BoE prudential oversight on HM Treasury recognition.

milestones.title: FCA selects Revolut for UK Regulatory Sandbox stablecoin cohort
milestones.description: Revolut chosen alongside Monee Financial Technologies, ReStabilise, and VVTX from a pool of 20 applicants to test stablecoin issuance under proposed UK rules; testing began Q1 2026.

milestones.title: Revolut granted full UK banking licence by PRA
milestones.description: PRA and FCA lift mobilisation restrictions after a 20-month phase; banking services move to Revolut Bank UK Ltd, but any GBP stablecoin would be issued from Revolut Ltd (the e-money entity) per BoE's proposed rule prohibiting the same group from issuing stablecoins across affiliated subsidiaries.

milestones.title: Revolut UK Head of Policy testifies to House of Lords on GBP stablecoin strategy
milestones.description: Rory Tanner tells peers the UK is 'already behind' the US and EU; outlines UK→India remittance corridor (seventh-largest globally) as priority B2B use case; flags Bank of England's proposed 'branded stablecoin' ban as a commercial blocker.

milestones.title: Bank of England signals stablecoin proposals were 'excessively conservative'
milestones.description: Deputy Governor Breeden indicates the BoE is ready to soften its proposed stablecoin rules following industry pushback, ahead of revised draft rules, easing the 'branded stablecoin' ban and holding-cap risks flagged for GBP issuers like Revolut.

milestones.title: Bank of England drops £20k individual holding cap for aggregate issuer caps
milestones.description: At CityWeek 2026 the BoE confirms it is abandoning the proposed £20,000 per-person holding limit in favour of aggregate issuance caps; revised draft rules expected June 2026.

milestones.title: House of Lords committee urges BoE to drop individual holding limits and reconsider 40% reserve floor
milestones.description: The Financial Services Regulation Committee called on the Bank of England to scrap per-person stablecoin holding limits entirely and reconsider the 40% unremunerated-reserve requirement, warning it would harm issuer viability.

milestones.title: Bank of England publishes final policy statement and draft rules on systemic stablecoins
milestones.description: The BoE scrapped individual holding limits in favour of a temporary per-coin issuance cap (initially ~£40bn / $50bn), raised the maximum short-dated-UK-T-bill reserve share from 60% to 70% (remainder held at the BoE, no yield to holders), and required par redemption within 24 hours. A Code of Practice consultation runs to September 22 2026, with rules finalised by end-2026 and regulated sterling stablecoins operating from 2027.

milestones.title: Bank of England and FCA publish joint approach to regulating systemic stablecoin issuers
milestones.description: The FCA will regulate qualifying stablecoins issued from UK establishments from October 25 2027. The Bank of England takes prudential oversight once HM Treasury recognises an issuer as systemic, using Banking Act section 191 powers of direction for case-by-case transition. The Code of Practice is to be finalised by end-2026.

milestones.title: Revolut ships its first stablecoin in euro (EURR), with no sterling equivalent announced
milestones.description: Revolut launches EURR on Ethereum under MiCA, issued by Bridge Building S.A. rather than a Revolut entity, phased to Denmark, Poland, and Portugal. The launch demonstrates Revolut's issuance model is a third-party regulated-issuer relationship, but no GBP token was announced. GBPR remains gated on the UK regime, whose Code of Practice consultation runs to September 22 2026 with rules finalised by end-2026.

milestones.title: UK Treasury plans a secondary Bank of England objective to support stablecoin innovation
milestones.description: The Treasury plans an amendment to the Financial Services and Markets Bill adding a Bank of England secondary statutory objective to support innovation in stablecoins and other digital money, with annual reporting to Parliament, while keeping financial stability primary. The Code of Practice consultation closed September 22 with finalisation still targeted by end-2026 and the FCA regime effective October 25 2027; no Revolut GBP token was announced.

milestones.title: FCA opens authorisation gateway for the UK cryptoasset regime, including stablecoin issuance
milestones.description: The FCA's application period for the new UK cryptoasset regime, which covers issuing qualifying stablecoins, opened on September 30 2026 and runs to February 28 2027. The regime comes into force in October 2027. Revolut has not said whether it has applied.

name: HKDAP
launchPhaseDetail: HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer FRS01, effective April 10 2026; JV between Standard Chartered, HKT, and Animoca Brands; 1:1 backed by HKD-denominated high-quality liquid assets, which Standard Chartered Trustee (Hong Kong) Limited holds on trust for HKDAP holders. On May 13 2026, Anchorpoint, OSL Group, and PantherTrade completed a full-lifecycle test transfer on Ethereum mainnet (fiat funding, reserve, mint, transfer, full redemption) without putting tokens into circulation, confirming Ethereum as the deployment chain. The original end-of-Q2 2026 phased rollout target closed on June 30, 2026 with no public circulating token. On July 21 2026 Caixin reported, citing people familiar with the plans, that Anchorpoint will launch HKDAP within the month with distribution through licensed exchanges OSL and HashKey, which are already testing payment and fund use cases. The July window then closed without a launch: on August 3 2026 Standard Chartered CEO (HK) Mary Huen said work continues since the April licence, public-blockchain testing is ongoing, and the HKDAP launch announcement is now expected within August 2026, with a B2B2C distributor model whose distributor list follows the formal launch. The August window was met: on August 11 2026 OSL Group announced it was among the first key authorised distributors under an HKDAP beta access programme, and on August 12 2026 HashKey Exchange joined as a distributor and reported completing an initial mint-and-redemption cycle including fiat conversion both ways. Access is restricted to institutions, corporate clients, and professional investors, with retail targeted no earlier than late 2026, a target CEO Dominic Maffei declined to reaffirm on October 25 2026. Anchorpoint's own release of August 12 2026 announced the phase 1 rollout through Beta Access for institutional distributors and professional investors. Anchorpoint disclosed neither the first-transaction value nor the admitted client count, but the deployment is now identified: HKDAP is an upgradeable ERC-20 at 0x87622385F960fcCB3121d6D0A9513bd1D9Bed6cA on Ethereum (6 decimals, name "HKD At Par"), carrying a supply of 527,199.52 HKDAP as of August 29 2026, which held flat through August 31 and then rose across the first week of September to 698,833.91 HKDAP (about $89.1K) on September 6 2026 and 875,549.91 HKDAP (about $111.6K) on September 12 2026, then 1,006,889.91 HKDAP (about $128.3K) on September 20 2026, flat since September 18. On September 14 2026 Payment Asia Group reported the first named commercial use: a full fund-mint-pay-reconcile-redeem-burn cycle with OSL as distributor, settling ShipAny logistics fees and Flow hospitality employee benefits, without disclosed amounts. Standard Chartered became the first bank distributor on August 24 2026, with Finloop, Yunfeng Financial, and a Bank of East Asia memorandum following on August 25-28, and on September 15 2026 Anchorpoint launched the Tokenised Money Adoption Programme with PwC Hong Kong as inaugural strategic partner. Supply reached 1,006,889.91 HKDAP (about $128.3K) on September 27 2026, roughly double August 27, with ten holder addresses and no remediation of the BlockSec findings announced. It then rose to about 16.1 million HKDAP by October 23 and, after Ethereum mints of about 87.0 million on October 30, to 103,102,419.91 HKDAP across 14 holders on November 1 2026. Anchorpoint's transparency page reported 103,404,235 HKDAP in circulation against 104,520,931 of reserves as of November 18 2026. On August 14 2026 BlockSec published a contract review reporting that the KYC proof argument is discarded so any proof passes, that de-registering a compromised KYC provider does not stop wallets it onboarded, that a single key can mint, burn, pause, or freeze while two keys control all upgrades and roles, and that debug logging, a zero-run optimizer, and uploaded test files suggest a pre-production build was deployed to mainnet. DefiLlama began tracking HKDAP as stablecoin id 437 on August 27 2026, reporting circulating supply consistent with the on-chain figure. Supply is therefore now measurable, but no accepted source returns a price: the DefiLlama list price field is null, coins.llama.fi resolves neither the Ethereum contract nor the CoinGecko id, and anchorpoint-hkd-at-par remains a preview listing with zero supply and no platforms. Pharos holds HKDAP pre-launch until a fetchable price path exists.

milestones.description: OSL Group announces it is among the first key authorised distributors for HKDAP under Anchorpoint's beta access programme, with intended use cases spanning tokenised funds, trade finance, and cross-border payments. milestones.description: Anchorpoint began the phase 1 rollout of HKDAP via Beta Access for institutional distributors and professional investors, after minting and live transfer tests on a public blockchain in the second quarter. Authorised distributors convert between HKDAP and fiat for institutions, corporate users and professional investors; broader retail adoption is targeted as early as end-2026, depending on market conditions.
