milestones.description: HashKey Exchange joined OSL Group as an authorised HKDAP distributor and reported completing an initial minting and redemption cycle for eligible clients, including fiat conversion into and out of the stablecoin. Circulating supply, first-transaction value and admitted client count were not disclosed.

milestones.title: BlockSec publishes HKDAP contract security review flagging KYC and key-control defects
milestones.description: BlockSec reports that the KYC proof argument is passed in but discarded so any proof including an empty string passes, that an isActive logic error lets wallets onboarded by a de-registered KYC provider keep transacting, and that a single key can mint, burn, pause, or freeze while two keys control all upgrades and roles, with no timelocks or multi-signature requirements on high-risk operations. Debug logging left in the proxy fallback, an optimizer set to zero runs, and test files uploaded to Etherscan indicate a pre-production build was deployed to mainnet.

milestones.title: Standard Chartered becomes the first bank distributor of HKDAP
milestones.description: Standard Chartered announced it will distribute HKDAP to corporate and institutional clients, the first bank to take a distributor role, widening a network that already included OSL Group and HashKey Exchange; Anchorpoint's press page then added Finloop (August 25), Yunfeng Financial (August 26), and a Bank of East Asia memorandum (August 28).

milestones.title: DefiLlama begins tracking HKDAP, giving the token its first public circulating-supply figure
milestones.description: DefiLlama adds HKDAP as stablecoin id 437 (peggedHKD, fiat-backed), reporting circulating supply of roughly 527,200 HKDAP. The figure matches the on-chain total supply of the Ethereum deployment at 0x87622385F960fcCB3121d6D0A9513bd1D9Bed6cA. No price field is populated on the listing.

milestones.title: Payment Asia settles logistics and hospitality invoices in HKDAP through OSL
milestones.description: Payment Asia Group announced a completed business-to-business settlement cycle using HKDAP with OSL Group as distributor and Anchorpoint as issuer: fiat funding, minting, payment, same-day reconciliation, redemption, and burn. Use cases named are service-fee settlement with logistics partner ShipAny for POS terminal deliveries and employee benefits through the hotel booking agency Flow. No transaction values or client counts were disclosed, and the release gives no retail timing.

milestones.title: Anchorpoint launches Tokenised Money Adoption Programme with PwC Hong Kong as inaugural partner
milestones.description: Anchorpoint announced TAP, an industry initiative for education, research, and dialogue on tokenised money in Hong Kong, with PwC Hong Kong signing on as inaugural strategic partner. HKDAP remains in institutional beta; no retail launch, contract upgrade, or BlockSec remediation accompanied the programme.

milestones.title: HKDAP circulating supply roughly doubles to about 1.01 million HKDAP; still no price field
milestones.description: DefiLlama stablecoin id 437 and the Ethereum contract both show 1,006,890 HKDAP outstanding on September 27 2026, up from about 527,200 on August 27, across ten holder addresses, including a one-day 3.16 million mint-and-burn snapshot on September 25 that reverted within a day. DefiLlama's price field remains null and CoinGecko carries a preview listing with zero supply, so no runtime price path exists.

milestones.title: Finloop and QFPay HK complete an HKDAP payment transaction with Anchorpoint
milestones.description: Finloop Finance, an HKDAP distributor, and payment provider QFPay HK announced a collaboration with Anchorpoint and a completed payment transaction using HKDAP. No amount was disclosed.

milestones.title: HKDAP supply rises to about 16.1 million
milestones.description: DefiLlama shows HKDAP circulating supply stepping from about 1.0 million to about 6.1 million on October 3 2026 and to about 16.1 million on October 23 2026. DefiLlama still carries no price for HKDAP.

milestones.title: Anchorpoint CEO declines to reaffirm end-2026 retail target
milestones.description: Chief executive Dominic Maffei said Anchorpoint still intends to offer HKDAP to retail users on a public blockchain but declined to confirm a launch date or reaffirm the previous target of retail access as early as the end of 2026, days after HSBC launched RedCoin on PayMe. Institutional beta access continues.

milestones.title: Anchorpoint and Solana Foundation plan native HKDAP minting and redemption on Solana
milestones.description: Anchorpoint announced its first collaboration with a public blockchain foundation: HKDAP is to be natively minted and redeemed on Solana, supporting retail access, payments and tokenised RWA use cases. No launch date was given; HKDAP remains in institutional beta on Ethereum.

milestones.title: Anchorpoint partners with Mastercard and Visa to explore HKDAP settlement
milestones.description: Anchorpoint announced strategic partnerships with Mastercard and Visa to explore enabling HKDAP as a supported stablecoin on both card networks, starting with settlement options for card issuers. Mastercard said it would explore HKDAP use cases through its Global Money Platform, which combines its payments network with BVNK's stablecoin infrastructure. The release gives no launch date or volumes.

milestones.title: HKDAP circulation rises to about 103.1 million
milestones.description: Anchorpoint's weekly transparency figures as of October 30 2026 show 103,102,420 HKDAP in circulation against reserves of 104,206,693, with 103,496,769 issued and 1,501,270 redeemed over the prior 30 days. Ethereum mints of about 87.0 million HKDAP on October 30 account for the rise from about 16.1 million. DefiLlama tracks the same supply but still carries no price for HKDAP.

milestones.title: Anchorpoint completes self-hosted wallet verification pilot
milestones.description: Anchorpoint completed an Open Wallet Verification Framework pilot with Terminal 3 for HKDAP transfers from self-hosted wallets.

name: HSBC RedCoin
launchPhaseDetail: HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer FRS02, effective April 10 2026. HSBC named the token HSBC RedCoin on September 30 2026 and launched it on October 23 2026 under the ticker RCHKD, available on PayMe by HSBC (3.3M users) for peer-to-peer and merchant payments, with HSBC Digital Assets Custody providing safekeeping. On November 19 2026 HSBC added RedCoin wallets to the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App, where eligible customers can use RCHKD to subscribe to a tokenized unit class (Class SD) of its Hong Kong dollar money market fund. 1:1 backed by HKD-denominated high-quality liquid assets in segregated accounts. HSBC now publishes issuer-reported circulation and reserve figures; its 21 November 2026 daily update showed HK$592.8 million outstanding against HK$593.8 million of cash reserves. Pharos keeps RCHKD in pre-launch until public on-chain issuance and a verifiable price and supply path exist.

milestones.title: HKMA grants stablecoin issuer licence to HSBC
milestones.description: The HKMA grants The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited a stablecoin issuer licence under the Stablecoins Ordinance, effective April 10 2026.

milestones.title: HSBC names its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin HSBC RedCoin
milestones.description: HSBC named its planned HKD stablecoin HSBC RedCoin and stated that at launch it will be offered only through PayMe and the HSBC HK Mobile App, restating a launch plan for the second half of 2026.

milestones.title: HSBC RedCoin (RCHKD) launches on PayMe
milestones.description: HSBC made HSBC RedCoin, ticker RCHKD, available on PayMe by HSBC from October 23 2026 under its HKMA stablecoin issuer licence, with HSBC Digital Assets Custody providing safekeeping. HSBC plans to add stablecoin wallet functionality to the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App later in 2026. The release names no blockchain and gives no circulation or reserve figures.

milestones.title: HSBC daily disclosure shows HK$81.4 million RedCoin outstanding against HK$82.4 million of cash reserves
milestones.description: HSBC's daily stablecoin disclosure reported HK$81,425,493.24 of RedCoin outstanding and HK$82,425,493.24 of reserve assets, all held as cash, with the circulating total up HK$80,157,394.18 over seven days. The figures are issuer-reported and unaudited; the first independent reserve audit is expected after Q4 2026, and RCHKD still runs on HSBC's private permissioned ledger with no public price or supply lane.

milestones.title: HSBC reports 50,000 RedCoin users after launch
milestones.description: HSBC group CEO Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong FinTech Week that RedCoin had about 50,000 users since its October 23 launch.

milestones.title: HSBC RedCoin goes live in the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App with tokenized fund access
milestones.description: HSBC made RedCoin (RCHKD) available in the HSBC HK Mobile Banking App, where eligible customers can activate a stablecoin wallet and use RCHKD to subscribe to Class SD, a tokenized unit class of the HSBC Global Money Funds Hong Kong dollar fund, from HKD 100. RedCoin still runs on HSBC's own DLT network rather than a public blockchain.

name: OKRW
launchPhaseDetail: First sovereign L1 blockchain (Maroo) purpose-built for KRW stablecoins; testnet live May 2026; dual-track regulated and open paths; Hashed's testnet release says mainnet will follow security audits and gives no date; OKRW is planned as a won-pegged stablecoin, but no issuer has been named and Tiger Research reported on September 17 2026 that issuer eligibility was still under discussion. Pharos cleared the 2026 expectation on November 15 2026 because no Hashed or Maroo source states a mainnet year.

milestones.title: Hashed Open Finance publishes Maroo litepaper with OKRW as the network's stablecoin
milestones.description: Hashed Open Finance released a litepaper for Maroo, a Korean won focused Layer 1 whose network fees are paid in a won stablecoin, with separate open and regulated paths.

milestones.title: Maroo L1 testnet launches with OKRW as native KRW stablecoin
milestones.description: First sovereign L1 blockchain purpose-built for KRW stablecoins; dual-track regulated and open paths.

name: ARC
launchPhaseDetail: Pitched as India's first regulated rupee stablecoin, according to a CoinDesk report citing unnamed sources; built by Anq with Polygon; 1:1 INR collateralized by cash, fixed deposits, and government securities; designed to prevent USD liquidity outflow; two-tier framework complementing RBI's CBDC; Uniswap v4 whitelisting for compliance. The tentative January 2026 debut has passed with no RBI confirmation, no live circulating supply, and no ARC mention on anq.finance. Its status was uncertain as of mid-2026. In July 2026 the RBI signaled to a Parliamentary Standing Committee that it favors barring banks and regulated entities from exposure to private stablecoins, including rupee-backed ones, putting the project's regulated-INR-stablecoin premise in question. As of September 13 2026 anq.finance still carries no ARC mention; the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance rescheduled its Department of Economic Affairs evidence session on virtual digital assets to September 16 2026. No source supports a 2026 launch, so Pharos removed the expectation on September 13 2026

milestones.title: ARC rupee stablecoin announced by Anq and Polygon
milestones.description: Pitched as India's first regulated INR stablecoin, according to a CoinDesk report citing unnamed sources; collateralized by cash, fixed deposits, and government securities; January 2026 debut targeted.

milestones.title: RBI signals preference to bar regulated entities from private stablecoins, including rupee-backed
milestones.description: The RBI told a Parliamentary Standing Committee it leans toward prohibiting banks and regulated firms from crypto and private-stablecoin exposure, citing seigniorage and stability concerns. This directly constrains ARC's regulated INR-stablecoin model.

name: B3 BRL Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Latin America's largest stock exchange (B3/Sao Paulo) is developing B3RL, its own BRL settlement stablecoin for tokenized-asset trading. At B3's Tokenization Day (May 26-27 2026), coverage indicated a later-2026 / H2 2026 window for B3RL and the tokenized-asset registry; the prior H1 2026 window elapsed with no on-chain deployment visible. At Expert XP on July 23-24 2026 B3 placed the launch between August and September 2026, and its Q2 2026 results note (August 11) confirmed infrastructure testing of B3RL had begun, the first B3-owned confirmation of the ticker. That window also lapsed: at B3 Week on September 15 2026 digital-assets director Felipe Paiva said infrastructure for new use cases, including tokenized collateral, would be ready at the start of 2027, and September reporting frames B3RL as a 2027 launch. Backing is mainly cash and Tesouro Nacional securities, with Polygon named in Brazilian press and by Paiva. No deployment was visible as of September 27 2026, and Pharos moved the expected launch to 2027 on September 27 2026. On October 8 2026 B3 said B3RL will not settle the first tokenized shares targeted for early 2027 and that the settlement currency remains undecided. Pharos moved the launch phase from launching-soon to testnet on October 18 2026, reflecting infrastructure testing with no near-term settlement role.

milestones.title: B3 announces BRL stablecoin and tokenization platform
milestones.description: Latin America's largest stock exchange plans a BRL-pegged settlement stablecoin for tokenized asset trading.

milestones.title: B3 Tokenization Day: B3RL stablecoin and tokenized share registry confirmed for H2 2026
milestones.description: B3 confirmed its tokenized share registry and B3RL settlement stablecoin target H2 2026 (slipped from H1 2026); stablecoin to be backed by cash and government bonds.

milestones.title: B3 clarifies B3RL settlement stablecoin targets H1 2026 on Polygon; tokenization platform follows in H2
milestones.description: At Tokenization Day, B3 OTC and digital-assets director Humberto Costa said the B3RL settlement stablecoin, backed by cash and government bonds, built on Polygon, is expected in the first half of 2026, while the tokenized-share registry/tokenizer advances in the second half, disentangling the two timelines that earlier coverage had merged.

milestones.title: B3 director confirms B3RL launches "in the coming months" at Expert XP 2026
milestones.description: Director Felipe Paiva said B3 launches B3RL in the coming months, with asset tokenization to follow in early 2027; corroborated by Jornal do Comércio on July 24.

milestones.title: B3 narrows the B3RL launch window to August-September 2026
milestones.description: Coverage of Expert XP 2026 reports B3 director Felipe Paiva placing the B3RL launch between August and September 2026, with backing mainly in cash and Tesouro Nacional securities and tokenised assets to follow in early 2027.

milestones.title: B3's Q2 2026 results note confirms infrastructure testing of B3RL has begun
milestones.description: B3's own Bora Investir results summary states the company started testing the infrastructure of B3RL, its stablecoin, as a step toward asset tokenisation. It is the first B3-owned source to name the B3RL ticker.

milestones.title: B3 Week: B3RL still in testing; tokenization infrastructure readiness targeted for early 2027 as the August-September window lapses
milestones.description: At B3 Week 2026, digital-assets director Felipe Paiva said B3 is advancing its platform, the B3RL stablecoin (built on Polygon, backed mainly by cash and public securities), and tokenized instruments, and that at the start of next year B3 will be prepared to build new use cases including tokenized collateral. The August-September launch window stated at Expert XP in July passed with no deployment; reporting through September 21 frames B3RL as a 2027 asset.

milestones.title: B3 says B3RL will not settle the first tokenized shares
milestones.description: At an FGV event in Sao Paulo, B3 executive Humberto Costa said B3RL will not take part in the initial settlement of tokenized shares targeted for early 2027, that the settlement currency is still undecided between stablecoins, tokenized deposits and a possible Drex link, and that B3 will file a broad Central Bank crypto intermediation and custody license request before October 30.

name: Flipcash USDF
launchPhaseDetail: Debut token on Coinbase's Custom Stablecoin platform; went live 2026-05-20 on Solana, 1:1 backed by USDC, with Coinbase Onramp fiat access; serves as the settlement asset for Flipcash's user-created currencies; the on-chain reserve contract (github.com/code-payments/flipcash-program) was audited by Sec3. The Solana mint is 5AMAA9JV9H97YYVxx8F6FsCMmTwXSuTTQneiup4RYAUQ (6 decimals, pinned in the issuer's flipcash-program repository, created January 8 2026); it carried 2,875,649.80 USDF across 529 holders on September 13 2026, grew to 3,181,003.29 USDF by September 27, and fell to 2,686,924.32 USDF across 556 holders on October 25 2026. Jupiter lists one pool for the mint, created April 22 2026, with about $376 of liquidity and no price. USDF is not listed on DefiLlama's stablecoin list or on CoinGecko. In July 2026 Coinbase's exchange still listed USDF as operational-only backend testing (no trading, deposits, or withdrawals), while the token itself circulates on Solana.

milestones.title: Coinbase enables USDF for operational testing
milestones.description: Coinbase enabled USDF for operational testing only; trading, deposits, and withdrawals were unavailable.

milestones.title: USDF goes live on Solana via Coinbase's Custom Stablecoin platform
milestones.description: Flipcash launches USDF, 1:1 USDC-backed, on Solana with Coinbase Onramp fiat access.

milestones.title: USDF supply reaches 3.18 million on Solana with still no market, price feed, or trading launch
milestones.description: On-chain supply at the Coinbase Custom Stablecoins mint grew about 10.6 percent in two weeks, from 2,875,650 USDF on September 13 to 3,181,003 on September 27. Jupiter lists no pair for the mint, CoinGecko has no entry, and no trading launch or platform news accompanied the growth.

name: RD Technologies HKDR
launchPhaseDetail: Issued by RD InnoTech Limited (a subsidiary of RD Technologies, founded by former HKMA chief executive Norman Chan); admitted to the HKMA stablecoin issuer sandbox in the first July 2024 cohort. Raised $40M in Series A2 (July 30 2025, led by ZA Global) and signed a Memorandum of Understanding with ZA Bank for HKDR reserve custody and potential distribution pending regulatory approval, the first major collaboration between a licensed HK virtual bank and a stablecoin development company. Hong Kong Stablecoins Ordinance took effect August 1 2025; 36 formal applications were received by the September deadline. HKMA granted its first two stablecoin licences on April 10 2026 to Anchorpoint Financial (FRS01) and HSBC (FRS02). RD InnoTech was not in the first batch. HSBC plans its HKD stablecoin launch for H2 2026; a second licence wave is expected and RD InnoTech, with its early sandbox participation, $40M war chest, and ZA Bank partnership, remains among the credible next-round candidates. HK$25M minimum paid-up capital and 100%+ reserve backing requirements already met under sandbox conditions. As of September 13 2026 the HKMA register (last revised April 23 2026) still lists only the two April licensees, and RD Technologies' 2026 press releases cover Africa expansion and awards without mentioning HKDR. No source supports an H2 2026 launch, so Pharos removed the expectation on September 13 2026.

milestones.title: RD InnoTech enters HKMA Stablecoin Issuer Sandbox (first cohort)
milestones.description: HKDR begins sandbox testing for digital asset trading and cross-border trade payments under HKMA supervision.

milestones.title: Cobo designated preferred wallet partner for HKDR custody infrastructure
RD InnoTech names HashKey Exchange as distribution partner; Ethereum confirmed as deployment chain
Hong Kong Stablecoins Ordinance passed; takes effect August 1 2025
milestones.description: Legislative Council passes the Stablecoins Ordinance, mandating HKMA licensing for issuers of fiat-referenced stablecoins; RD Technologies welcomes the framework.

milestones.title: RD Technologies closes $40M Series A2 financing
milestones.description: Eight-investor round led by ZA Global alongside China Harbour, Bright Venture, Hivemind Capital, HSG, Eternal Digital, CMSC Partners, and Guotai Junan International PE; announced one day before the Stablecoins Ordinance licensing regime took effect.

milestones.title: ZA Bank signs MOU for HKDR reserve custody and potential distribution
milestones.description: ZA Bank (subsidiary of ZA Global, Hong Kong's first licensed virtual bank) will explore reserve asset custody services and a potential distribution role for HKDR, pending regulatory approval; first major collaboration between a licensed HK virtual bank and a stablecoin development company.

milestones.title: Hong Kong Stablecoins Ordinance licensing regime takes effect
milestones.description: HKMA formally opens licensing for issuers of fiat-referenced stablecoins; 36 formal applications received by the September 30 2025 deadline.

milestones.title: HKMA confirms first batch of stablecoin licences targeted for March 2026
milestones.description: Eddie Yue signals stability over speed and limits initial licences to 'a very small number'; RD InnoTech named among credible candidates given early sandbox participation.

milestones.title: HKMA grants first two stablecoin licences to HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial; RD InnoTech not in first batch
milestones.description: HKMA awards FRS01 to Anchorpoint Financial Limited and FRS02 to HSBC after receiving 36 applications. RD InnoTech was among the 5 original sandbox participants but was not licensed in this first wave. HSBC plans H2 2026 for its HKD stablecoin launch.

milestones.title: HKMA confirms further stablecoin licence applications under review with no set timetable
milestones.description: In a LegCo LCQ6 reply, the HKMA said the remaining licence applications stay under review with an open-but-cautious stance and no timetable for further grants, leaving RD InnoTech's licence, and any HKDR launch window, unconfirmed.

name: BRD Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Announced Jan 6 2026 on 'Cripto na Real' by former Brazil central bank deputy governor Tony Volpon (BCB 2015-16, ex-UBS/Nomura MD); to be issued by CF Inovacao (co-founded with Jose Carneiro in 2023), targeting institutional investors who want on-chain access to Selic-rate yield (~15%); positioned as the first BRL-pegged token to explicitly share government-debt yield with holders, competing against Crown's BRLV which raised a $13.5M Series A from Paradigm in December 2025; no formal product docs or deployment timeline yet; the BCB framework from Public Consultations 109-111 is now in force as Resolutions 519/520/521 (effective February 2 2026); BCB Resolution 561 (published Apr 30 2026, effective Oct 1 2026) further bans stablecoin/crypto settlement in regulated cross-border FX, tightening the regulatory backdrop. As of September 13 2026 the CF Inovacao website lists no BRD product page and no source has given a timeline, so Pharos removed the 2026 expectation

milestones.title: Tony Volpon unveils BRD yield-sharing BRL stablecoin on 'Cripto na Real'
milestones.description: Former BCB deputy governor announces CF Inovacao-issued BRD, backed by Brazilian government debt with Selic-rate yield distributed to holders; positions BRD against existing BRL stablecoins and Paradigm-backed Crown BRLV.

milestones.title: Brazil stablecoin FX-classification regime takes effect
milestones.description: BCB resolutions classifying stablecoin transactions as foreign-exchange operations enter force.

milestones.title: BCB Resolution 561 bans stablecoin settlement in regulated cross-border FX
milestones.description: Brazil's central bank publishes Resolution 561 (effective Oct 1 2026) prohibiting authorised FX providers from using stablecoins or crypto to settle cross-border remittances, a restrictive backdrop for BRD, though it does not name CF Inovacao.

name: BDACS KRW1
launchPhaseDetail: Production KRW1 contracts on Ethereum, Avalanche and Arc have issued tokens on-chain since the first Ethereum mint on July 10 2026, following the September 2025 proof of concept, while BDACS ties full commercial issuance to Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act. BDACS is South Korea's regulated digital-asset custodian; Woori Bank holds the won reserves and participated directly in the PoC. Initial deployment on Avalanche (cited by KISA for reliability in public-sector use); KRW1 expanded to Polygon in December 2025 for broader payments, remittances, and enterprise reach. October 2025 MoU with Circle positions KRW1 for deployment on Arc (Circle's new Layer 1), where it joins national stablecoin issuers from Japan, Brazil, Mexico, and the Philippines. February 2026 Plume partnership positions KRW1 as Korean institutional settlement rail for tokenized RWA. May 2026 Aptos Foundation partnership brings KRW1 to its first non-EVM chain, leveraging Aptos's payment infrastructure for cross-border remittances and RWA tokenisation. A February 2026 MoU with Com2uS Holdings targets KRW1-based payment infrastructure on the XPLA/CONX chain. KRW1 is live on Aptos with 30M tokens per rwa.xyz, which reported 141.8M KRW1 (about $97K) across Polygon, Aptos, Plume, Ethereum, and BNB Chain with 33 holders on September 13 2026. On September 7 2026 BDACS adopted LayerZero's OFT standard to unify that supply across chains, and on September 8 agreed card-payment rails with XBITU. Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act (the gate for commercial launch) was excluded from the National Assembly's pre-recess agenda on May 12 2026; the first public hearing planned for late September was effectively cancelled on September 22 2026 after the government bill was delayed, with the FSC targeting a November subcommittee and year-end passage uncertain. September 2026 brought a dense partnership run (Rain/Visa card rails, Arc mainnet at launch, Fireblocks custody) alongside scrutiny of the 2026 whitepaper's claim that KRW1 is a commercial product in operation, which BDACS said it would review; commercial launch remains contingent on the unenacted framework. On October 18 2026 Pharos replaced the registry's zero-supply proof-of-concept Ethereum and Avalanche contracts with the July 2026 production contracts named in BDACS's September 2026 accountant reserve report (Ethereum, Avalanche and Arc, 18 decimals), linked DefiLlama id 429 and CoinGecko id krw1, and dropped the BSC, Polygon and Plume proof-of-concept rows that krw1.kr lists as PoC only. After a 19.56 million burn on October 30, the production contracts held 6,208,284 KRW1 across Ethereum, Avalanche and Arc on November 1 2026. DefiLlama counts only the 4,010,046 KRW1 on Ethereum. A BDACS official told Seoul Economic Daily, via Decenter, on November 5 2026 that issuance and burning take place continuously in proof-of-concept exercises and that the October 30 burn was also part of a test.

milestones.title: BDACS trademarks KRW1 brand
milestones.description: BDACS files KRW1 trademark and begins building issuance infrastructure ahead of formal Korean stablecoin regulation.

milestones.title: KRW1 proof-of-concept goes live on Avalanche with Woori Bank
milestones.description: Successful PoC validates fiat deposits, on-chain issuance, and real-time banking-API reserve attestation; not yet in public circulation.

milestones.title: BDACS signs MoU with Circle to bring KRW1 to Arc blockchain
milestones.description: BDACS and Circle formalize collaboration to deploy KRW1 on Arc, Circle's new Layer 1 blockchain (public testnet); KRW1 becomes the first Korea-based issuer on the network, joining issuers from Japan, Brazil, Mexico, and the Philippines.

milestones.title: KRW1 launches on Polygon network
milestones.description: Multi-chain expansion following the Avalanche PoC; Polygon selected for high throughput, low fees, and integrations with Stripe, Circle, and Mastercard, enabling payments, remittances, and enterprise use cases.

milestones.title: KRW1 deploys on BNB Chain
milestones.description: Multi-chain expansion to BNB Chain; on-chain BEP-20 contract live (0x8c2f2784cbab626846a53d20d8104ff42b3594c2).

milestones.title: BDACS partners with Plume to position KRW1 as Korean institutional RWA settlement rail
milestones.description: Plume integration lets Korean institutional investors allocate into tokenized RWA instruments denominated in KRW1 without USD conversion; ~$645M of tokenized assets currently on Plume.

milestones.title: BDACS and Com2uS Holdings sign MoU to build KRW1 payment infrastructure on XPLA/CONX
Korea Digital Asset Basic Act excluded from National Assembly pre-recess agenda; H2 2026 earliest for resumed debate
BDACS and Aptos Foundation partner to bring KRW1 to Aptos
milestones.description: First deployment of KRW1 outside EVM-compatible chains; aims to accelerate practical stablecoin use cases across domestic and global markets via Aptos's low-fee payment infrastructure for remittances and real-world asset tokenisation.

milestones.title: BDACS publishes institutional KRW1 whitepaper
milestones.description: Institutional whitepaper published on the BDACS newsroom; krw1.kr now describes commercialization of issuance and circulation for select KYC/AML-vetted institutions, while aggregator-tracked supply remains proof-of-concept scale pending Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act (bills introduced July 28 2026).

milestones.title: First production KRW1 mint on Ethereum
milestones.description: The production Ethereum contract 0xb83fc84df7028251066c25f5d61d12fd9d9c8be4 minted its first 1,000,000 KRW1 on July 10 2026, the start of public on-chain issuance from the July 2026 production deployments.

milestones.title: Korea's finance ministry targets Digital Asset Basic Act passage in the second half of 2026
milestones.description: The Ministry of Economy and Finance set a target of passing the Digital Asset Basic Act in H2 2026, the framework that would authorise won-pegged stablecoin issuers and gate KRW1's commercial launch. The Bank of Korea and the Financial Services Commission remain split over whether issuance should be restricted to bank-majority entities.

milestones.title: Unified Digital Asset Basic Act bill still not introduced; first public hearing set for late September
milestones.description: National Policy Committee chair Yoo Dong-soo says the FSC's government bill has not yet arrived, ten private-member bills remain pending, and the bank 50%-plus-one consortium rule is unresolved. The Democratic Party plans a first public hearing at the end of September 2026.

milestones.title: BDACS adopts LayerZero's OFT standard to run KRW1 as a single omnichain supply
milestones.description: LayerZero says KRW1 will use the Omnichain Fungible Token standard for one unified supply across connected chains, with Stargate executing transfers. The post lists KRW1 as live on Ethereum, Avalanche, and Circle's Arc.

milestones.title: BDACS and XBITU agree to build KRW1 card-payment rails
milestones.description: Singapore-based XBITU is to enable KRW1 spending at Visa and Mastercard merchants and through Apple Pay and Google Pay via automatic conversion, starting with a domestic beta. No launch date was given.

milestones.title: BDACS partners with Rain to make KRW1 spendable across Visa's card network
milestones.description: BDACS said it partnered with payments-infrastructure firm Rain to link KRW1 to Visa's global card payment network, with Rain handling Visa issuance and settlement and BDACS handling KRW1 issuance and custody; rollout is staged pending foreign-exchange legislation.

milestones.title: KRW1 whitepaper draws scrutiny for describing the token as 'a commercial product actually in operation'
milestones.description: Seoul Economic Daily reported that BDACS's 2026 institutional whitepaper markets KRW1 as already operating commercially under its existing virtual-asset-service-provider filing accepted by KoFIU, drawing criticism that this conflates a VASP filing with issuer status under a law that has not passed, with shareholder Woori Bank reportedly unaware; BDACS said it would review whether to revise the wording. On-chain supply remains at proof-of-concept scale, about 141.8 million KRW1 (roughly $97K) across chains.

milestones.title: KRW1 joins Circle's Arc mainnet at launch as the only Korean won stablecoin
milestones.description: At Arc's mainnet launch, KRW1 went live as the only won stablecoin on Circle's new Layer 1, converting the October 2025 testnet cooperation into a production integration; BDACS plans KRW1-based on-chain FX using Circle's StableFX and reports integrations across Ethereum, Avalanche, Arc, Plume, Polygon, BNB Chain, and Aptos.

milestones.title: BDACS selects Fireblocks for institutional custody supporting KRW1
milestones.description: BDACS announced Fireblocks as its custody infrastructure for stablecoin transactions and cross-chain operations for institutional clients; BDACS reported more than 80 billion won in assets under custody in the first half of 2026.

milestones.title: Digital Asset Basic Act September public hearing effectively cancelled; FSC now targets a November subcommittee
milestones.description: The public hearing expected around September 30 fell through after the government bill was delayed, leaving year-end passage uncertain; the FSC still aims for a National Assembly bill-review subcommittee in November. The framework that would authorise won-pegged issuers, and therefore KRW1's commercial launch, remains unenacted.

milestones.title: BDACS demonstrates a testnet KRW1 to USDC swap through Circle StableFX
milestones.description: At the Korea Blockchain Week side event Bridging Finance Onchain, co-hosted with Circle, Kyobo Life and SBI Holdings, BDACS demonstrated an onchain exchange and settlement of KRW1 against USDC using Circle's StableFX institutional FX program in a testnet environment.

milestones.title: Injective and BDACS sign MoU on KRW1 as won settlement asset
milestones.description: Injective and BDACS signed a memorandum of understanding aiming to make KRW1 the exclusive won-denominated settlement asset for real-world assets on Injective. Minting and redemption are limited to approved institutional partners and remain subject to regulatory approval. No launch date was given.

milestones.title: KRW1 supply falls to 6.21 million after a 19.56 million burn
milestones.description: On October 30 2026, 9.66 million KRW1 on Ethereum and 9.9 million KRW1 on Avalanche moved from one address to a second address and were burned within five minutes. Supply across the Ethereum, Avalanche and Arc production contracts fell from about 25.77 million to 6.21 million KRW1.

milestones.title: BDACS describes October burn as proof-of-concept testing
milestones.description: A BDACS official told Seoul Economic Daily, via Decenter, that issuance and burning take place continuously in proof-of-concept exercises and that the October 30 burn was also part of a test.

name: Revolut USD Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Companion to the already-tracked RGBP (Revolut GBP). Revolut secured a MiCA CASP licence from Cyprus (CySEC) on Oct 23 2025. In October 2025, Revolut launched fee-free 1:1 USD↔stablecoin swaps (USDC/USDT on Ethereum, Solana, and Tron) for its 65M users; stablecoin payment volumes on the platform surged 156% in 2025 to ~$10.5B. In February 2026, the FCA selected Revolut as one of 4 firms (from 20 applicants) for a UK stablecoin payment testing pilot, though that sandbox is specifically for a GBP token, not USD. Revolut received a full UK banking licence from the PRA (Mar 11 2026) and filed an OCC national bank charter application for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Mar 5 2026, targeting a 2027 US launch with built-in stablecoin access). Revolut's stablecoin programme shipped on August 26 2026, but in euro rather than dollars. EURR launched on Ethereum in a phased rollout to Denmark, Poland, and Portugal, with Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui support planned, alongside the removal of Tether's USDt from Revolut's European retail offering by August 31 2026. EURR is issued by Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg entity of Stripe-owned Bridge, with Revolut Digital Assets Europe authorised through CySEC. Revolut's Lithuanian EMI was not the issuer of record, contrary to earlier reporting. On September 2 2026 the OCC granted preliminary conditional approval for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Corporate Decision #1390), with opening targeted for the first half of 2027; the decision records that the bank plans to offer Revolut-branded stablecoins through a third-party issuer and will not manage reserves, matching the Bridge template used for EURR. Pharos moved the expected launch to 2027 on September 13 2026 on the strength of the OCC timeline. Revolut's EEA cryptocurrency terms of September 15 2026 name USDR alongside EURR as Revolut-branded e-money tokens, with Bridge Building S.A., an EMI authorised by Luxembourg's CSSF under licence W00000024, as sole legal issuer and Revolut Digital Assets Europe, the CySEC-authorised CASP, acting only as offeror. The terms say each Revolut EMT is offered only once its white paper is published. As of October 30 2026 ESMA's register held no USDR white paper, and no USDR contract, chain or launch date had been published.

milestones.title: Revolut Digital Assets Europe receives MiCA CASP licence from CySEC
milestones.description: Revolut's Cyprus entity gets MiCA authorisation to passport regulated crypto services across the EEA; unveils 'Crypto 2.0' platform with 1:1 stablecoin/USD conversion as a flagship feature.

milestones.title: EU counsel describes a Revolut USD/EUR stablecoin in 2026 as 'plausible' under MiCA
milestones.description: Decrypt reports Revolut's Lithuanian EMI provides the EMT issuer foundation; Cyprus CASP licence is the service-provider side; sources say Revolut has been working on its own stablecoin for over a year.

milestones.title: FCA selects Revolut for UK stablecoin payment testing pilot
milestones.description: Revolut is one of 4 firms chosen from 20 applicants to trial stablecoin products in real-world UK conditions from Q1 2026; use cases include stablecoin payments, wholesale settlement, and crypto trading. Results will inform the FCA's crypto regulatory framework targeting October 2027.

milestones.title: Revolut files OCC national bank charter application (Revolut Bank US, N.A.)
milestones.description: Revolut applies for a US national bank charter with a $500M investment commitment, targeting a 2027 US bank launch with built-in stablecoin access (third-party USDC/USDT, not confirmed own issuance).

milestones.title: Revolut receives full UK banking licence from the PRA
milestones.description: Revolut exits mobilisation; 13M UK customers gain FSCS protection. A GBP stablecoin would be issued from Revolut's e-money entity, not the UK bank.

milestones.title: Revolut confirms its planned US national bank will offer stablecoin services alongside FDIC-insured accounts
milestones.description: Reuters reports Revolut Bank US, N.A. (OCC charter applicant) will offer stablecoin services alongside FDIC-insured products from day one, though own-issuance of a Revolut USD token remains unconfirmed; the USD path continues to run through the Lithuanian EMI / MiCA EMT route.

milestones.title: Revolut launches EURR euro stablecoin issued by Stripe's Bridge, not its Lithuanian EMI
milestones.description: Revolut ships the first token of its stablecoin programme as the euro-denominated EURR on Ethereum, phased to customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal with wider EEA availability planned later in 2026. The token is issued by Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg entity of Stripe-owned Bridge, under MiCA, with Revolut Digital Assets Europe authorised through CySEC, correcting the prior assumption that Revolut would issue e-money tokens from its own Lithuanian EMI. Support for Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui is planned, and Revolut applies no spread or fee on euro-to-EURR conversion. No USD-denominated equivalent was announced.

milestones.title: Revolut completes removal of Tether USDt from its European retail offering
milestones.description: Revolut finishes the phased withdrawal of USDt for European retail customers that began in July 2026, coinciding with the EURR rollout and leaving MiCA-compliant tokens as the euro-stablecoin option on the platform.

milestones.title: OCC conditionally approves Revolut Bank US; stablecoins to be issued by a third party
milestones.description: OCC Corporate Decision #1390 grants preliminary conditional approval to charter Revolut Bank US, N.A., subject to at least $95M paid-in capital, FDIC insurance, and Federal Reserve approval; management targets opening in the first half of 2027. The decision states the bank plans to offer Revolut-branded stablecoins through a third party, will not be the issuer, and will not manage any reserves, limiting its role to marketing, access, and custody via Revolut Ltd.

milestones.title: Revolut's EEA crypto terms name USDR as a Bridge-issued e-money token
milestones.description: Revolut Digital Assets Europe's cryptocurrency terms for the EEA define EURR and USDR as the Revolut-branded e-money tokens, with Bridge Building S.A. as legal issuer and Revolut Digital Assets Europe acting only as offeror. Holders may redeem a Revolut EMT directly from Bridge at par and free of charge. As of October 30 2026 ESMA's register listed only EURR for Bridge, and no USDR white paper, contract or launch date had been published.

name: Revolut Euro
launchPhaseDetail: EURR is live, not forthcoming. Pharos tracks it pre-launch only because it is not yet admissible to runtime data. Revolut launched the token on August 26 2026 as the first product of its stablecoin programme, in euro rather than the dollar or sterling tokens it had been expected to ship first. The issuer of record is Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg entity of Stripe-owned Bridge, holding an EMI licence and MiCA authorisation from the CSSF; Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd distributes the token under its own CySEC MiCA licence. This is a third-party issuer relationship, not in-house issuance from Revolut's Lithuanian EMI as earlier reporting had assumed. The token is an ERC-20 at 0x8e9c32a536ab623a2e0e9961bce6f5fe7504e084 on Ethereum (6 decimals, name "Revolut Euro"), with a second deployment on Polygon at 0x11b20f798b70df2201D8F550ADDcc3378b33dd4A holding 3 EURR, and Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui listed as intended networks in the MiCA white paper. That white paper set the public offer start at August 20 2026, six days before the app rollout. Rollout is phased, reaching Denmark, Poland, and Portugal first with wider EEA availability targeted later in 2026, and Revolut charges no spread or fee on euro-to-EURR conversion. Supply grew from 366 EURR to 250,957 EURR in the first two days, held flat through August 31, then rose again through the first week of September to 1,671,782.16 EURR (about $1.94M) on September 6 2026, and has since moved less than 2,000 EURR: 1,674,912.63 on September 12 and 1,676,863.60 on September 27. DefiLlama began tracking EURR as stablecoin id 436 on August 27 2026 and now carries that supply, but its price field is null. CoinGecko's revolut-euro has since picked up the Ethereum contract mapping and the matching total supply, yet it remains a preview listing returning no price and no market cap, /simple/price returns an empty object, and coins.llama.fi resolves neither the contract nor the CoinGecko id. Supply is measurable; no accepted source returns a fetchable price, so Pharos holds EURR pre-launch until a price path exists. Bridge's reserve page (reserves.bridge.xyz/eurr, updated September 27 2026) reports 1,676,867 EURR outstanding against EUR 1,676,867 of reserves held entirely as cash deposits at credit institutions; Ernst & Young S.A. issued a reasonable-assurance report on the reserves report as of August 31 2026, and the reserve page on October 25 2026 reported 1,689,252 EURR against EUR 1,689,252 of cash deposits. Ernst & Young S.A.'s reasonable-assurance report, signed October 30 2026, shows 1,676,866.60 EURR against EUR 1,676,868.90 of cash and cash equivalents held at Banking Circle in Luxembourg as of September 30 2026.

milestones.title: Bridge's MiCA white paper sets the EURR public offer start at August 20 2026
milestones.description: The white paper, notified to ESMA on July 23 2026, names Bridge Building S.A. (CSSF EMI W00000024, CASP N00000012) as issuer and Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd as co-offeror through the Revolut app and Revolut X. Holders may redeem at par to an EEA IBAN within two business days at no fee. The paper lists Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui as intended networks.

milestones.title: Revolut launches EURR on Ethereum, issued by Stripe's Bridge under MiCA
milestones.description: Revolut ships the first token of its stablecoin programme as the euro-denominated EURR, phased to customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal with wider EEA availability planned later in 2026. Bridge Building S.A. is the issuer of record under a Luxembourg EMI licence and MiCA authorisation from the CSSF, with Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd distributing under its CySEC MiCA licence. Support for Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui is planned, and Revolut applies no spread or fee on euro-to-EURR conversion.

milestones.title: EURR deployed on Polygon alongside Ethereum
milestones.description: Polygon Labs confirms the Polygon deployment at 0x11b20f798b70df2201D8F550ADDcc3378b33dd4A. On-chain supply on Polygon was 3 EURR on September 13 2026, so the Ethereum contract carries effectively all circulating supply.

milestones.title: DefiLlama begins tracking EURR with no price field populated
milestones.description: DefiLlama adds EURR as stablecoin id 436 (peggedEUR, fiat-backed). Circulating supply rises from 366 EURR to roughly 250,957 EURR within two days, matching the on-chain total supply of the Ethereum deployment. The listing reports a null price, and CoinGecko's revolut-euro entry remains a preview listing, so no fetchable price path exists.

milestones.title: Revolut completes removal of Tether USDt from European retail alongside the EURR rollout
milestones.description: Revolut finishes the phased withdrawal of USDt for European retail customers that began in July 2026 with a purchase freeze and deposit block, leaving MiCA-compliant tokens including its own EURR as the euro-stablecoin option on the platform.

milestones.title: Ernst & Young attests EURR reserves as of August 31 2026
milestones.description: Ernst & Young S.A. performed a reasonable assurance engagement on Bridge Building S.A.'s EURR reserves report as of August 31 2026.

milestones.title: Bridge reserve page reports 1,674,916 EURR fully backed by cash deposits
milestones.description: Bridge's live EURR reserve disclosure shows 1,674,916 EURR outstanding against EUR 1,674,916 of reserves, 100% in cash deposits at credit institutions and 0% in highly liquid financial instruments, with redemption routed through redeem.bridge.xyz. Supply has been effectively flat since September 6 2026 (1,671,782 to 1,674,913 EURR). No fetchable price path exists yet.

milestones.title: Ernst & Young reports EURR reserves held at Banking Circle
milestones.description: Ernst & Young S.A. signed a reasonable-assurance report on Bridge Building S.A.'s EURR reserves as of September 30 2026. The report shows 1,676,866.60 EURR backed by EUR 1,676,868.90 in cash and cash equivalents held at Banking Circle in Luxembourg.

name: Euro eXchange Token
launchPhaseDetail: EURXT is live on Ethereum mainnet. Pharos tracks it pre-launch only because no admitted source prices it. Crédit Agricole S.A. announced the launch on July 1 2026. CACEIS issues the token, a first issuance settled a subscription to a tokenised Amundi money market fund, and the token is initially made available to CACEIS's institutional investor and corporate clients. The issuer of record is CACEIS Bank S.A. (LEI 96950023SCR9X9F3L662), an ACPR-authorised credit institution that CACEIS says is directly supervised by the European Central Bank. Its MiCA white paper, notified to the ACPR on April 3 2026, offers EURXT only to professional clients of CACEIS Bank with a 10,000 EURXT minimum, and ESMA's interim MiCA register lists the white paper with a June 30 2026 notification date. The token is the ERC-20 at 0xf62dc56438f13e9cd8076b7d6cf3e616cf756cd0 (name "Euro eXchange Token", 6 decimals), named in the white paper and on stable-xt.io. It was deployed behind a transparent upgradeable proxy on June 2 2026, and its implementation has not been upgraded since. The client restriction governs purchases from and redemptions with the issuer. Holding is open: the white paper says any ERC-20 wallet can hold EURXT unless sanctioned or otherwise restricted, OpenZeppelin's audit describes transfer checks limited to a pause and a sender and recipient blacklist, and simulated transfers from the current holder to two unused addresses succeeded at block 26319420. Issuance is public on chain. After a first 10,000 EURXT mint on June 12 2026, burned the same day, supply stood at 20,020,000 EURXT on launch day. Blockscout then records repeated cycles in which 25 million to 33.4 million EURXT were minted, transferred and burned at the issuer's redemption address, and supply has held at 54,366,000 EURXT since September 25 2026. At block 26319420 (November 1 2026) one externally owned account, 0x2a394a2486cf53e45d31721344acde1f3bed6398, held the entire supply. CoinGecko's euro-exchange-token entry maps the contract and reports that supply, but it is a preview listing with null price and market cap and no tickers. DefiLlama does not list EURXT, and coins.llama.fi returns no quote for the contract. On October 29 2026 CACEIS said it expects listings on several centralised exchanges against BTC, ETH and USDC by the end of 2026.

milestones.title: CACEIS Bank notifies the EURXT white paper to the ACPR
milestones.description: The MiCA white paper names CACEIS BANK S.A., a French credit institution, as issuer of a euro e-money token on Ethereum. It offers EURXT only to professional clients of CACEIS Bank with a 10,000 EURXT minimum subscription, gives holders par redemption with no fee from 9:00 to 17:00 on French bank business days, and lists pause, blacklist, freeze and fund-recovery functions in the token contract.

milestones.title: OpenZeppelin audit of EURXT finds three low-severity issues
milestones.description: OpenZeppelin reviewed the EURXT contract on May 20 and 21 2026 and reported no critical, high or medium findings. The report describes six access-control roles, a global pause, a sender and recipient blacklist checked in the transfer hook, and a seizure path that moves a blacklisted balance to another address. CACEIS said fixes for the three low findings would ship in the version deployed at launch, and Deloitte issued an agreed-upon procedures report on the contract on May 29 2026.

milestones.title: ESMA's interim MiCA register lists CACEIS Bank's EURXT white paper
milestones.description: The e-money token register entry names CACEIS BANK SA (LEI 96950023SCR9X9F3L662), a credit institution with the ACPR as competent authority, with digital token identifier 2GPH3VZ45, white paper link stable-xt.io and a notification date of June 30 2026. ESMA's comment records an ongoing additional review of the white paper's qualitative information.

milestones.title: Crédit Agricole launches EURXT with a tokenised Amundi fund subscription
milestones.description: Crédit Agricole S.A. announces EURXT, an ERC-20 euro e-money token issued on Ethereum by CACEIS and backed 1:1 by reserves held as cash on CACEIS Bank's balance sheet. A first issuance settled a subscription to a tokenised Luxembourg-domiciled Amundi UCITS money market fund, and the token is initially available to CACEIS's institutional investor and corporate clients.

milestones.title: EURXT supply settles at 54.37 million after September mint cycles
milestones.description: A 34,346,000 EURXT mint to 0x2a394a2486cf53e45d31721344acde1f3bed6398 at block 26053523 and a 66,670,000 EURXT burn at the redemption address at block 26053743 left total supply at 54,366,000 EURXT, all held at that one address. Supply was unchanged at block 26319420 on November 1 2026.

milestones.title: CACEIS plans EURXT exchange listings against BTC, ETH and USDC
milestones.description: CACEIS says EURXT is available to its clients that hold a wallet with a regulated crypto-asset service provider, a custody service CACEIS itself offers under MiCA, and that clients can buy or sell EURXT free of charge through its interface. It expects listings on several centralised exchanges against BTC, ETH and USDC by the end of 2026, and use as a settlement asset on permissioned DLT trading and settlement systems.

name: Aplauz WEUR
launchPhaseDetail: The current whitepaper, amended 24 August 2026, states in Part G that WEUR has not yet launched or entered circulation. The homepage offers account creation, issuance and redemption and claims public on-chain verification, creating a lifecycle ambiguity without independently verified production contracts or circulation. Whitepaper publication and offer-start on 8 July are not confirmed issuance dates. ESMA records whitepaper notification on 25 June 2026, separately from its 26 May last-update field. No confirmed launch date is published. The whitepaper gives WSPN as Aplauz NL B.V.'s trading name and WSPN Fintech Dutch Holding B.V., a holding entity in the Worldwide Stablecoin Payment Network group, as its direct parent, which acquired the company during 2024 and 2025 with DNB approval. It names Ethereum (ERC-20) and BNB Smart Chain as the initial launch networks.

milestones.title: ESMA records WEUR whitepaper notification
milestones.description: Notification is not whitepaper approval or evidence of circulation.

milestones.title: Whitepaper publication and offer-start date
milestones.description: The disclosed offer date does not establish public token issuance.

milestones.title: Amended whitepaper states WEUR has not launched

name: Quantoz PLNQ
launchPhaseDetail: Quantoz announced PLNQ on April 14 2026 with Zodia Markets supporting initial distribution, and PLNQ is deployed on Ethereum, but the issuer states no tokens are in circulation and no reserve exists. Ethereum block 26107706 observed 2026-10-02 confirms symbol PLNQ, six decimals and zero totalSupply; the exact-contract DefiLlama price response is empty. The whitepaper plans Polygon, Algorand, XRP Ledger and Xahau, but those production identities are not verified. No CoinGecko identity or launch date is published. The cover states original AFM notification on 6 April 2026, while ESMA records notification on 7 April and the whitepaper was amended on 30 April.

milestones.title: Whitepaper cover states original AFM notification
milestones.description: The document I.01 field instead gives 6 March; the cover date is retained as an attributed statement.

milestones.title: ESMA records PLNQ whitepaper notification
milestones.description: Not a confirmed circulation date or approval of the whitepaper.

milestones.title: Quantoz Payments announces PLNQ and GBPQ
milestones.description: Quantoz announced PLNQ and GBPQ as MiCA electronic money tokens to be issued initially on Ethereum, with Polygon, Stellar, XRPL, Algorand and Xahau planned later and Zodia Markets supporting initial institutional distribution. The release gives no circulation figure.

milestones.title: PLNQ whitepaper amended to version 1.1

name: CZKC Czech Koruna
launchPhaseDetail: CZKC a.s., company number 19989971, invites public testnet use and describes CZK-backed tokens. Its about page says WBTCB, a Czech crypto-trading holding company, stands behind CZKC. Martin Stránský first presented CZKC publicly in E15's KryptoSpace podcast of 22 June 2023. Developer documentation lists Ethereum, Arbitrum and Gnosis but marks all production and public-testnet addresses to be published. CzechInvest named CZKC among 21 sandbox testing projects on 3 February 2026; participation is not MiCA authorization. On 22 June 2026 the Czech National Bank reported that no entity in the Czech Republic had yet obtained an e-money institution licence to issue koruna-pegged e-money tokens. A confirmed commercial launch date remains unverified.

milestones.title: World BTC owner Martin Stránský presents the CZKC koruna stablecoin
milestones.description: Martin Stránský, owner of the World BTC group, presented CZKC on E15's KryptoSpace podcast as a koruna stablecoin issued only against matching koruna reserves. He said the code was practically finished, an external audit was planned and the Czech National Bank required an e-money institution licence.

milestones.title: Founder says CZKC will seek a full e-money licence
milestones.description: Martin Stránský told Forbes Czech Republic that about a month earlier he had decided to seek a full e-money institution licence from the Czech National Bank, rather than a small-scale licence capped at five million euros. He said the team aimed to file the application in the first third of December 2023 and could, with luck, obtain the licence within six months.

milestones.title: CzechInvest names CZKC in sandbox testing cohort
milestones.description: Dated programme milestone, not an inferred first token announcement or issuance authorization.

milestones.title: Czech National Bank reports no koruna e-money token licence yet
milestones.description: The Czech National Bank's spring 2026 Financial Stability Report states that no entity in the Czech Republic has yet obtained an e-money institution licence authorising issuance of koruna-pegged e-money tokens. The report does not name CZKC.

name: Itau Unibanco BRL Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Itau Unibanco (Brazil's largest private bank by assets, ~5.6T BRL) is evaluating its own stablecoin. Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes confirmed exploration at an industry event in Sao Paulo in April 2025: 'we are always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. Brazil's virtual-asset framework (Consultas Publicas 109-111) was finalised as BCB Resolutions 519, 520, and 521 in November 2025 and took effect on February 2 2026; peg-currency choice (BRL or USD) and product timeline remain undisclosed. Itau participated in the DREX wholesale CBDC pilot, gaining distribution-rail experience; ticker not yet announced. Pharos tracks BRL as the most likely first launch given the Brazilian retail base, but the editorial summary documents the open USD option. BCB Resolution 561, dated April 30 2026, bars virtual assets in payments or receipts between an eFX provider and its foreign counterparty from October 1 2026. It does not name Itau. At Blockchain.RIO on August 13 2026 Antunes said stablecoins and tokenised deposits must coexist, without committing to an Itau-issued token. No source has given a launch timeline since the April 2025 remark, so Pharos removed the 2026 expectation on September 13 2026.

milestones.title: Itau Unibanco confirms it is evaluating its own stablecoin
milestones.description: Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes tells a Sao Paulo industry event Itau is exploring a BRL or USD stablecoin pending BCB regulation under Consulta Publica 111.

milestones.title: Brazil stablecoin FX-classification regime takes effect
milestones.description: Regime in force; Itau's launch timing remains contingent on the Consulta Publica 111 framework.

milestones.title: BCB Resolution 561 restricts virtual assets in eFX settlement
milestones.description: BCB Resolution 561, dated April 30 2026, bars virtual assets in payments or receipts between an eFX provider and its foreign counterparty from October 1 2026. It does not name Itau.

milestones.title: Itau named among 140+ businesses signed up to use Open USD
Itaú digital-assets head reiterates watchful stance; no own-stablecoin decision
milestones.description: Guto Antunes told BitNotícias that Itaú's crypto client base grew 252 percent since the December 2024 retail expansion and that the bank is closely tracking tokenization and stablecoins as potential enablers of new payment models. The Drex pilot has ended; no issuance decision, peg choice, ticker, or date has been announced.

name: iM Bank KRW Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: South Korea's first bank-led KRW stablecoin proof-of-concept; built by iM Bank and Finger on the Kaia blockchain; features quantum-resistant (PQC) security via BTQ Technologies and Keypair. BTQ's Q1 2026 filing reports the precursor Finger pilot completed 1,477 production transactions at 100% success with 200+ post-quantum wallets, and names iM Bank as its lead commercial conversion candidate. The May 2026 OpenAsset full-lifecycle PoC issued and transacted iMKRW on Kaia. The separate July 2026 Coocon payment-ecosystem PoC used BEATOZ blockchain and CPG technology; its release did not identify Kaia or name the token iMKRW. Pharos marks the phase testnet; these are private pilots, not a public testnet. In June 2026 iM Bank joined the Korea-EU Pangea project testing KRW-EUR stablecoin exchange with Shinhan, K Bank, Qivalis, Swift, and Chainlink. Commercialization remains gated on Korean stablecoin legislation, which had not been introduced as a unified bill as of September 2026, and the production symbol/ticker is not yet confirmed. iM Bank has announced no launch date, and issuance awaits the Digital Asset Basic Act.

milestones.title: iM Bank signs won stablecoin agreement with Finger and Validator
milestones.description: iM Bank signed a memorandum of understanding with fintech firm Finger and blockchain firm Validator to build bank-led won stablecoin issuance and distribution infrastructure, starting with a proof of concept that reconciles bank deposits against on-chain issuance in real time. iM Bank is to hold and certify the reserves, Finger to link existing financial systems, and Validator to handle global infrastructure and distribution.

milestones.title: iM Bank and Finger announce first bank-led KRW stablecoin PoC on Kaia
milestones.description: Pilot features quantum-resistant security via BTQ Technologies' post-quantum cryptography stack.

milestones.title: iM Bank and OpenAsset complete technical PoC issuing 'iMKRW' on Kaia
milestones.description: Controlled-environment proof-of-concept with OpenAsset's OpenMint solution demonstrated the full token lifecycle (issuance, top-up, QR payment, merchant settlement, and burn) across 80+ scenarios. A separate partner track from the Finger/BTQ post-quantum security pilot.

milestones.title: iM Bank joins the Korea-EU 'Pangea' stablecoin remittance project
milestones.description: Launched in Zurich with Shinhan Bank, K Bank, Qivalis, Swift, Chainlink, and FairSquareLab, the project is to test direct exchange between KRW and EUR stablecoins for remittance, FX, and settlement. iMKRW is not named in the announcement.

milestones.title: Coocon, iM Bank, and Beatoz complete stablecoin issuance and payment-ecosystem PoC
milestones.description: Payment APIs bridged bank infrastructure and the Beatoz CPG blockchain, covering policy-fund execution via smart contracts and regional payment infrastructure. No commercialization timeline given.

milestones.title: Digital Asset Basic Act September public hearing effectively cancelled; FSC now targets a November subcommittee
milestones.description: The public hearing expected around September 30 fell through after the government bill was delayed amid a prolonged presidential policy-director vacancy, leaving year-end passage uncertain; the FSC still aims for a National Assembly bill-review subcommittee in November. The licensing framework gating iMKRW commercialisation remains unenacted.

name: KB Kookmin KRW stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: KB Financial Group's May 17, 2026 release records a completed issuance, offline payments, merchant settlement and Vietnam remittance proof of concept with KG Inicis, Kaia and OpenAsset, including Hollys kiosk QR payments. Kaia identifies KB Kookmin as the bank pilot participant on its network. Commercial services are conditional on Korean digital-asset legislation; no launch date is announced. Final product name, legal issuer and official ticker are unpublished. KRW-KB is an editorial display label, not an issuer-assigned ticker. The closed pilot is not described as a public testnet or beta.

milestones.title: KB announces completed payments and remittance proof of concept
milestones.description: KB Financial Group describes the integrated won-token issuance, offline QR payments, smart-contract settlement and Vietnam bank-account receipt demonstration with KG Inicis, Kaia and OpenAsset. Actual services are planned for implementation of digital-asset legislation.

milestones.title: Kaia confirms KB Kookmin's May pilot
milestones.description: Kaia's Q2 report confirms that KB Kookmin and iM Bank separately piloted won-stablecoin offline payments, remittances and settlement on its network during May. It does not announce a publicly circulating KB token.

milestones.title: MoonPay names KB Kookmin Bank as a Korean stablecoin partner
milestones.description: MoonPay's Korea launch says KB Kookmin Bank will examine wallets, on and off ramps, stablecoin issuance and distribution, and overseas remittance with MoonPay, and KB Kookmin Card will test stablecoin payments by foreign visitors. The announcement is exploratory and gives no KB issuance date.

obituary.epitaph: Bankruptcy closed Fluid's dollar rail
obituary.obituary: Fluid Finance SA was dissolved by bankruptcy and renamed in liquidation effective 2024-04-22. Its DUSD and issuer websites no longer resolve, so Pharos freezes DUSD as an archived legacy asset rather than an active issuance venue.

obituary.epitaph: The ICON dollar retires with Balanced v1
obituary.obituary: Balanced v2 launched on April 7, 2026 and the original v1 app is no longer supported. Issuer documentation sets v1.balanced.network to go offline on December 1, 2026, after which outstanding loans are liquidated and the contracts are made inaccessible ahead of ICON's permanent shutdown at the end of 2026. bnUSD(old) migrates 1:1 into the separate new bnUSD, but only from ICON, Stellar and Sui; holders on the legacy bridge deployments must bridge there first. Reported circulating supply was about $938K at capture, below its recorded peak of about $1.17M. Pharos has published no market price since CoinGecko's last quote on June 26, 2026, found no DEX pairs, and freezes v1 as an archived legacy asset.

obituary.epitaph: Inter Protocol sunset by governance
obituary.obituary: In April 2025 a governance proposal to sunset Inter Protocol cited declining market appetite for decentralized stablecoins, rising operational complexity and costs, and a refocus on Agoric's Orchestration work and the BLD token. Agoric's on-chain signaling Proposal 93 passed on May 1, 2025, starting a planned 60-day wind-down: no new vault openings or IST minting, a liquidation fee set to zero so vault users could repay IST and reclaim collateral, and weekly liquidation-ratio increases to close any remaining vaults. The sunset concluded on July 1, 2025. Pharos keeps IST as a frozen archive because the former vault and PSM dollar stablecoin no longer operates as an active mintable protocol asset.

obituary.epitaph: Goal3 sunset its dollar with the protocol
obituary.obituary: Goal3 announced on 2024-06-19 that it was sunsetting the Goal3 Protocol and frontend, and told holders to redeem zkUSD for USDC as soon as possible. Supply has not changed since 2024-06-22 and the issuer's domains no longer resolve.

name: Gyndore
launchPhaseDetail: Protocol announced with whitepaper published; website live with core metrics showing 'Soon'. Claims audit-first approach but no specific auditor or report confirmed. A public waitlist opened May 21 2026 (waitlist.gyndore.com), reviving social activity after the GitHub repo (last commit Mar 7) and Medium (last post Feb 2) went quiet. A public testnet on Base Sepolia (chain 84532) is open to any EVM wallet using free test assets, running alongside the DropWave points campaign; the testnet was live by August 25 2026, though neither gyndore.com nor Medium records an opening date. The Gyndore Liquidity Bootstrapping Event opened on September 15 2026 to raise launch capital and by September 20 the app reported it 100% sold out with bGYND allocations distributed; GYND began trading on Hydrex Integral pools on Base on September 23 2026. That event was a capital raise rather than a mainnet date: gyndore.com now lists only the GYND token contract deployed on Base on September 11 2026, the docs audit page names Sherlock but says no reports are published yet, and no gynUSD contract or mainnet date has been published, so Pharos records no expected launch date. Two launch configurations planned: bootstrapping (team admin key for borrow rate, transitioning via one-time fee switch to GYND governance) or GYND-from-day-one.

milestones.title: Gyndore announced: whitepaper published
milestones.description: Bitcoin-backed CDP stablecoin protocol on Base announced by Ayeteasea, with whitepaper and website going live.

milestones.title: Public waitlist opened at waitlist.gyndore.com
