milestones.title: Public testnet open on Base Sepolia with the DropWave points campaign
milestones.description: Third-party coverage records the public testnet as live on Base Sepolia (chain 84532), open to any EVM wallet using free test assets, alongside the DropWave points campaign. The date is the first observed coverage; the issuer published no opening date.

milestones.title: GYND governance token contract deployed on Base mainnet
milestones.description: GyndToken (10,000,000 GYND, ERC-20 with Permit, source verified) was deployed at 0x6cD1C7D41F589b5Ce6b88B1c90bc2F29B0439Ea1 on September 11 2026 and is now listed on gyndore.com. No gynUSD or protocol contracts have been published. The docs name Sherlock as audit partner but state no reports are published yet.

milestones.title: Gyndore Liquidity Bootstrapping Event opens and sells out
milestones.description: The Gyndore app opened the Liquidity Bootstrapping Event, a capital raise for the GYND launch market and protocol-owned liquidity, on September 15 2026; the DropWave page now reports the allocation 100% sold out and bGYND allocations distributed to nominated wallets, with GYND markets to open on Hydrex at an unannounced date. It was the project's first dated commitment; mainnet gynUSD contracts remain unpublished.

milestones.title: Gyndore retires DropWave for the upcoming LNMS hub; gynUSD mainnet contracts still unpublished
milestones.description: app.gyndore.com/dropwave now redirects to LNMS, described as Gyndore's upcoming incentive hub for social rewards and community campaigns, closing out the liquidity-bootstrapping event that sold out on September 15. The contracts page still states the protocol is not live on Base mainnet, gynUSD addresses publish only at launch, and the Sherlock engagement has produced no published report; the GYND token holds 147 holders and has traded on Hydrex Integral pools since September 23.

name: Tether Georgian Lari Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Announced May 25 2026 as a joint Tether / Government of Georgia initiative to place the Georgian Lari on digital-asset rails; not a CBDC (distinct from the NBG's separate digital-lari pilot). Grounded in NBG Order No. 52/04 (March 6 2026), which lets licensed VASPs issue Lari-pegged stablecoins under 100% reserve backing, prior NBG consent, full redemption rights, and GEL 500,000 minimum issuer capital; framework built for compatibility with the US GENIUS Act. Endorsed by PM Irakli Kobakhidze and NBG Governor Natia Turnava. Tether signed an MOU with Georgia in June 2023 and has invested in CityPay.io (active at 2,000+ Georgian merchant locations); GEL₮ is stated to be issued on multiple blockchains. Chains, contract addresses, reserve disclosures, banking partners, and launch timing to be announced at a later stage.

milestones.title: National Bank of Georgia adopts stablecoin offering rule
milestones.description: NBG Order No. 52/04 approved the rule for a virtual asset service provider's initial offering of a stablecoin, effective on publication. It requires prior written NBG consent for any stablecoin offering in Georgia.

milestones.title: Tether and the Government of Georgia announce GEL₮
milestones.description: Joint initiative to issue a Georgian Lari-pegged stablecoin under the NBG's stablecoin framework; structure, rollout, and regulatory implementation to follow. Endorsed by PM Irakli Kobakhidze and NBG Governor Natia Turnava.

name: Tenbin Gold
launchPhaseDetail: Live on Ethereum mainnet since 2026-02-10, with KYC-gated mint and redemption (about $597K market cap, 139.74 tGLD, 72 holders on September 27 2026, up from ~54 tGLD and ~36 holders in June). tGLD is a synthetic gold debt-note from Tenbin AssetCo (BVI) SPC: USDC-collateralized with gold exposure hedged via CME futures, KYC-gated mint/redeem, redeemable in USD stablecoin (no physical metal). Its only on-chain pool is a dormant Uniswap V4 tGLD/USDC pool; since September 9 2026 1inch has also routed tGLD swaps against USDC quotes supplied by Tenbin itself. CoinGecko's tenbin-gold price ($4,272.46, $597,027 market cap, 139.74 circulating) updated same-day on September 27 2026 on $2.20 of 24-hour volume, so the feed is currently fresh while trading remains near zero; the 14-day price history endpoint returns no points, so freshness continuity is unproven and the gold price-freshness gate has not been re-run. On October 25 2026 CoinGecko's market cap was 54 hours old, so its supply lane fails freshness; live tracking begins once that lane is fresh. A staked variant stGLD (ERC-4626) exists, and sibling FX tokens tBRL and tMXN are now listed as Ethereum mainnet deployments in the Tenbin docs; in May 2026 Tenbin deprecated LayerZero following internal security audits and migrated tGLD (and the FX siblings) exclusively to Chainlink CCIP. Q3 2026 audit reports from Zellic and Verilog were published to the contracts repository on August 26 2026; remediation fixes landed through August 31, and v1.5.1 and bug-bounty information followed on September 14. Since September 15 2026 a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed on Base has published Tenbin's attested off-chain reserve figure, a single total across all Tenbin assets, and the docs name Ripple Prime (formerly Hidden Road) as digital asset custodian.

milestones.title: Security audits completed
milestones.description: Independent audits by Spearbit, Fuzzland, Verilog, and 0xleastwood, alongside Certora formal verification.

milestones.title: $7M seed led by Galaxy Ventures
milestones.description: Galaxy Ventures led a $7M seed with Wintermute Ventures, FalconX, GSR, Nascent, Variant, Archetype, and Bankless Ventures.

milestones.title: tGLD deployed to Ethereum mainnet (private beta)
Tenbin adopts Chainlink CCIP for cross-chain expansion
JPEG Trading launches RWA curation with tGLD as inaugural Euler asset
milestones.description: JPEG Trading launched an RWA curation business with tGLD as its inaugural curated asset, deploying the first DeFi lending vaults for tGLD on Euler with co-deployed capital.

milestones.title: Q3 2026 audits by Zellic and Verilog published with remediation reports
milestones.description: Reports dated August 3 2026 (Zellic final, Verilog marked draft) with remediation notes were added to the tenbin-contracts repository on August 26 2026, followed by fix commits through August 31. Whether the remediated contracts are deployed on mainnet is not stated.

milestones.title: tGLD, tBRL and tMXN become swappable through 1inch
milestones.description: 1inch announced that Tenbin's Ethereum ERC-20 tokens tGLD, tBRL and tMXN can be swapped through its aggregator, with Tenbin quoting liquidity against USDC. 1inch states it is not the issuer and makes no representation about price tracking or collateralization.

milestones.title: Tenbin ships v1.5.1 and a bug bounty after landing audit remediations
milestones.description: Following the August 3 audit publications, Tenbin landed Verilog remediation fixes from August 21 to 31, including P0 and P1 severity items, then tagged v1.5.1 and added bug-bounty information on September 14. The beta float is unchanged at 139.74 tGLD with 72 holders on September 27, and CoinGecko's tenbin-gold price updated same-day on $2.20 of 24-hour volume.

milestones.title: Tenbin publishes off-chain reserves through a Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed
milestones.description: Tenbin's documentation describes an attested snapshot of off-chain reserves held at Ripple Prime, computed inside a Google Cloud Confidential Space enclave and published on Base through Chainlink's Tenbin Aggregated Off-Chain Reserves feed (0x7b1C8C60c05913aF3Aa21BaE3B32A02Ab4f39Bd3). The feed's first round is dated September 15 2026 and covers all Tenbin assets together. On-chain vault collateral is excluded from the figure because it can be read directly on Ethereum.

name: Theo thGOLD
launchPhaseDetail: Theo announced thGOLD on January 27 2026 as a yield-bearing gold product tracking the MG999 Onchain Gold Fund (FundBridge Capital, Libeara tokenization), and that gold-leasing fund already backs thUSD's carry strategy. The token contract was deployed on Ethereum on September 15 2026 (0x610F0E33b0A6b3802ff29D3Cf6bBd9A0ACF784ed, 6 decimals, about 15,279 thGOLD supply on October 19 2026). Theo's current documentation, read October 19 2026, redefines the token: one thGOLD is one fixed troy ounce of physical gold held allocated or leased to institutional counterparties, it does not accrue, and lease income goes only to the separate sthGOLD vault. The 4-of-6 Operator Safe holds the minter role and a Timelock owns the UUPS proxies. Direct mint and redemption are documented as coming soon, and Theo claims thGOLD is available on secondary venues. Both current thGOLD holders are issuer wallets according to Theo's deployed-addresses page, so independent public circulation has not been established. CoinGecko's thgold listing carries no contract or price, so Pharos has no usable public price feed and keeps the coin pre-launch.

milestones.title: Theo introduces thGOLD, tokenized yield-bearing gold tracking the MG999 fund
milestones.description: Announcement describes gold-denominated loans to retailers through the MG999 Onchain Gold Fund operated by FundBridge Capital with Libeara tokenization, approximately 2% annual yield, a phased launch, and Phase 1 early access open to institutional partners and accredited investors.

milestones.title: thUSD launches with MG999 gold leasing as its primary yield source
milestones.description: The thUSD launch states that its gold carry strategy is powered by thGOLD and that gold is leased to retailers through the MG999 fund, confirming the underlying gold-lending fund is operational ahead of standalone thGOLD availability.

milestones.title: thGOLD token contract deployed on Ethereum
milestones.description: Theo's deployed-addresses documentation lists thGOLD at 0x610F0E33b0A6b3802ff29D3Cf6bBd9A0ACF784ed with the sthGOLD vault at 0x507243F439d65F64dfeE799159431E3A7e85A9C4; the token is a 6-decimal ERC-20 with one Operator-multisig minter. Direct mint and redemption against physical gold were still marked coming soon on October 19 2026.

name: EJPY
launchPhaseDetail: Announced May 13 2026 by Japan Blockchain Foundation Co., Ltd. (JBFD), operator of Japan Open Chain (JOC), as a trust-type JPY-pegged stablecoin. Structured as a Type III electronic payment instrument under Japan's Payment Services Act (exempt from the ¥1M/transaction cap that constrains fund-transfer-type issuers such as JPYC), with JBFD as settlor and reserves to be held by a licensed trust bank (trustee in active negotiation, not yet named). Targeted for issuance and circulation on JOC within FY2026 (through March 2027), with Ethereum next and broader multi-chain expansion under consideration; actual issuance and handling dates to be formally announced once determined. Aimed at B2B payments, remittances, and settlement. Reserve composition not yet disclosed.

milestones.title: Japan Blockchain Foundation decides to issue trust-type yen stablecoin EJPY
milestones.description: JBFD announces a trust-type JPY-pegged stablecoin for Japan Open Chain and Ethereum, with the trust scheme structure clarified and a trustee under negotiation; issuance targeted within FY2026.

milestones.title: JBF launches 'Stablecoin Pilot Partners' with Toshiba among 26 institutions using test EJPY
milestones.description: Japan Blockchain Foundation opened a free roughly six-month pilot program (September 2026 to February 2027) in which 26 enterprises, financial institutions, and local governments, including Toshiba, SCSK, Asahi Broadcasting, Hachijuni Nagano Bank, and Tagawa City, explore stablecoin use cases spanning remittances, B2B payments, RWA settlement, and Web3 using test EJPY tokens and JOC wallets. The trustee bank remains unnamed and commercial issuance is still targeted within FY2026 (through March 2027).

name: RAKBank AED Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: RAKBank (The National Bank of Ras Al Khaimah P.S.C.) received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the UAE on January 7 2026 to issue an AED-backed payment token (stablecoin), subject to completion of regulatory and operational requirements under the CBUAE Payment Token Services Regulation. Planned to be fully backed 1:1 by dirhams in segregated, regulated accounts with full redemption at par, audited smart contracts, and real-time reserve attestations, targeting digital payments, asset tokenization, and cross-border settlements. The first conventional commercial-bank AED payment token under the CBUAE regime, distinct from Zand AED, AE Coin (Al Maryah), and the FAB/ADQ/IHC dirham initiative. Article (2) of the regulation bars a bank from acting as a payment token issuer itself (it may set up a licensed subsidiary, affiliate or related entity to do so) and limits a licensed issuer to issuing Dirham Payment Tokens to UAE residents. Ticker, chains, issuing-entity structure, and launch timing not yet announced; a pilot phase will follow in due course.

milestones.title: CBUAE grants RAKBank in-principle approval to issue an AED-backed stablecoin
milestones.description: The Central Bank of the UAE grants RAKBank in-principle approval to issue a dirham-backed payment token under the Payment Token Services Regulation, subject to completing regulatory and operational requirements.

name: Zand AED
launchPhaseDetail: AEDZ is publicly issued on Ethereum and Solana. Pharos tracks it pre-launch because no source returns a price and no admitted supply path covers both deployments. Zand Bank announced on November 17 2025 that the Central Bank of the UAE had approved it to launch Zand AED, issued by its wholly owned subsidiary Zand Trust L.L.C S.O.C. Zand Trust states that it is licensed under the Payment Token Services Regulation, and Taurus says it supplies the issuance and wallet technology. The Ethereum contract, a CMTAT v3 token behind an upgradeable proxy, was deployed on November 26 2025 and first minted on December 9 2025, and the Solana Token-2022 mint followed on January 19 2026. Zand Trust's transparency page lists both deployments with 6 decimals. Onboarded institutions mint and redeem through Zand Bank's corporate platform, and the issuer says AEDZ is also available on partner exchanges. On November 1 2026 supply was 509,523,397.48 AEDZ on Ethereum and 496,776,867 AEDZ on Solana, 1,006,300,264.48 in total. Exactly 1,000,000,000 AEDZ of that sits in eleven wallets, five on Ethereum and six on Solana, that each received a single transfer on September 30 or October 7 2026 and have not moved it. The issuer counts these balances as circulating: its October 1 2026 attestation matched the full on-chain supply, and its daily feed showed 1.01 billion AEDZ on October 30 2026. The wallets that receive every mint hold about 2 million AEDZ. CoinGecko's zand-aed is a preview listing with no price, market cap or tickers, DefiLlama does not track AEDZ, and no DEX pool exists.

milestones.title: CBUAE approves Zand to launch the Zand AED stablecoin
milestones.description: Zand Bank announces that the Central Bank of the UAE has approved it to launch Zand AED, a multi-chain AED-backed stablecoin on public blockchains issued by its wholly owned subsidiary Zand Trust and backed one to one by AED reserves held in segregated, regulated accounts.

milestones.description: An upgradeable proxy over a CMTAT v3.0.0 implementation is deployed at block 23884215 with name Zand AED, symbol AEDZ and 6 decimals.

milestones.description: The Solana mint, created on January 19 2026 with on-chain metadata name Zand AED and symbol AEDZ, issues its first 100 AEDZ. A 200,000,000 AEDZ lot follows on February 3 2026.

milestones.description: Under ISAE 3000 (Revised), AJMS LG Management Consulting concludes that management's reserve assertions are fairly stated: AED 806,328,717.78 of eligible reserves against 806,300,260.48 AEDZ in circulation (416,273,390.48 on Ethereum and 390,026,870 on Solana), held as AED 690,000,000 in term deposits, AED 104,546,598.20 in CBUAE Monetary Bills and AED 11,782,119.58 in cash. The report is dated October 5 2026.

milestones.title: Zand Trust reports 1.01 billion AEDZ in circulation
milestones.description: The issuer's daily transparency feed shows 1.01 billion AEDZ in circulation against AED 1.01 billion of reserves, split into AED 0.85 billion cash and AED 0.16 billion UAE Monetary Bills. On-chain supply on November 1 2026 was 1,006,300,264.48 AEDZ, of which exactly 1,000,000,000 sat in eleven wallets that each received one transfer on September 30 or October 7 2026.

name: DDSC
launchPhaseDetail: DDSC is issued on ADI Chain mainnet, but ADI Chain is not in Pharos's chain registry, so Pharos records no launch phase and its deployment and supply cannot enter runtime data. IHC, ADQ and First Abu Dhabi Bank announced a CBUAE-regulated dirham stablecoin on the ADI blockchain on April 28 2025, then to be issued by FAB. The October 2025 white paper names the issuer AEDC Stable Coin L.L.C., owned by Sirius Investment Holding (34%), IHC Capital Holding (33%) and 1968B SPV (33%), and records CBUAE in-principle approval on September 1 2025. The DDSC site now names AEDC Stable Coin Network and Distribution L.L.C. as the licensed issuer, holding Stored Value Facilities licence 05.01.01.018.2026.01 and Payment Token Services licence 09.01.01.004.2026.01. The CBUAE approved DDSC to go live on February 11 2026, and the ADI Chain explorer shows the first mint on February 16 2026 at token contract 0x1211f0cfe66739433c1330e21f4951b80e813479 (6 decimals). Authorized Distribution Partners onboard holders after KYC/KYB checks. IHC reported an AED 110 million DDSC transaction on May 21 2026, and a CBUAE no-objection certificate of July 3 2026 allows DDSC on selected VARA-regulated exchanges once its requirements are met; no platform was named. On November 1 2026 on-chain supply was 48,280,499 DDSC across 87 addresses, matching the issuer's transparency feed, which shows 657 DDSC in the issuance vault; the contract had minted 345,731,009 DDSC and burned 297,450,510 since February 2026. DefiLlama lists DDSC as stablecoin 458 at the exact ADI contract, but on November 15 2026 its list price equalled the dirham's official peg of 3.6725 per US dollar to every published decimal, so it is not a DDSC market quote; CoinGecko has no listing. Its white paper calls it the Digital Dirham StableCoin, a separate instrument from the CBUAE's Digital Dirham CBDC.

milestones.title: IHC, ADQ and FAB announce a dirham-backed stablecoin on ADI blockchain
milestones.description: The joint release says the stablecoin will be fully regulated by the CBUAE, issued by First Abu Dhabi Bank subject to regulatory approval, and run on the ADI blockchain developed by the ADI Foundation, for consumers, businesses and institutions.

milestones.title: CBUAE grants the DDSC issuer in-principle payment token approval
milestones.description: The DDSC white paper (version 1.0, October 2025) states that AEDC Stable Coin L.L.C. secured in-principle approval as a payment token issuer under the Payment Token Services Regulation, approval number CB UAE/BIS-L/2025/4821, dated September 1 2025.

milestones.title: CBUAE approves DDSC to go live on ADI Chain
milestones.description: IHC, Sirius International Holding and First Abu Dhabi Bank announce that the Central Bank of the UAE has approved DDSC to go live on ADI Chain, an institutional Layer 2 developed by the ADI Foundation, for payments, settlement, treasury and trade flows, and say DDSC is expected to be made available to FAB customers through approved platforms.

milestones.title: First DDSC minted on ADI Chain mainnet
milestones.description: The ADI Chain explorer records a first mint of 999 DDSC to the issuance vault on token contract 0x1211f0cfe66739433c1330e21f4951b80e813479. A 110,175,000 DDSC mint followed on April 14 2026.

milestones.title: IHC executes an AED 110 million DDSC transaction on ADI Chain
milestones.description: IHC reports executing an AED 110 million (about USD 30 million) transaction using DDSC on ADI Chain and says the initiative has moved from development into live deployment.

milestones.title: CBUAE grants DDSC a no-objection certificate for VARA-regulated exchanges
milestones.description: The Central Bank of the UAE issues a no-objection certificate allowing DDSC to go live on selected VARA-regulated exchange platforms, subject to meeting its requirements, to extend DDSC beyond institutional settlement to retail, merchant and business payments. IHC reports more than AED 150 million transacted since launch; no platform is named.

milestones.title: Network International pilots DDSC payments at two UAE retailers
milestones.description: Network International announced an in-store DDSC payment pilot at Marks & Spencer in Dubai Festival City and LuLu Hypermarket in Abu Dhabi's Khalidiyah Mall.

name: BILS
launchPhaseDetail: Bits of Gold, a Tel Aviv-based licensed crypto broker/custodian operating since 2013, received full regulatory approval on April 28 2026 from Israel's Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority (CMISA) to issue BILS, the first regulated shekel-pegged stablecoin, following a two-year sandbox pilot approved in March 2024. Backed 1:1 by New Israeli Shekels held in segregated dedicated bank accounts within Israel (foreign custody excluded), audited by Ernst & Young, with Fireblocks custody/issuance infrastructure and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, issued on Solana via token extensions. The regulator mandates a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout (likely institutional/qualified participants first) before wide availability; no firm public-launch date set. On November 1 2026 the Solana mint (CDxFUPSRK4dC68jWV7SCPezU1vNYXz87Y6fjhhRvsuhd) still held 100,000 BILS, unchanged since August 6 2026, although 268 transactions touched the mint between October 23 and October 29 2026. A further 100,000 BILS were minted on November 15 2026, the first supply change since August, taking the Solana supply to 200,000 BILS. On November 1 the bils.co.il transparency page showed 100K ILS of BILS in circulation, matching the supply at that time, and 105K ILS in total reserves; its 1.1M figure is a fixed total-supply label on the Solana and Ethereum tabs that neither contract supports. The Ethereum address the site lists, 0x24B3785B4Ec3eBB20Af43Cc3A132D86e0b936171, is a test token named 'Test BILS ETH', so Pharos records no Ethereum deployment. On August 16 2026 Bits of Gold disclosed a breach of up to 250,000 customers' personal details through a third-party analytics provider, reporting it to CMISA with funds unaffected. The transparency page lists the EY Q3 2026 report as pending, and the white paper served as new in September 2026 is internally dated June 2025. CoinGecko carries the mint with no price or tickers. Distinct from Israel's broader Stablecoin Law, which remains in draft/public-comment stage. Pharos tracks the ILS peg as OTHER until shekel peg support is built.

milestones.title: Israel's Capital Market Authority approves Bits of Gold shekel stablecoin sandbox pilot
milestones.description: CMISA approves a regulatory sandbox pilot for a shekel-pegged stablecoin issued by Bits of Gold, to be launched on Solana via token extensions.

milestones.title: CMISA grants full approval for BILS limited launch
milestones.description: After a two-year pilot, the Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority grants Bits of Gold full approval to issue BILS under conditions including 1:1 backing, segregated Israeli reserves, and an EY audit, with a gradual small-scale rollout.

milestones.title: Bits of Gold announces move to wide distribution of BILS
milestones.description: Official blog post states the sandbox pilot is complete and BILS is moving to wide distribution, with a live purchase and transparency site at bils.co.il; roughly 100,000 BILS minted on Solana as of early August 2026.

milestones.title: Bits of Gold discloses customer-data breach through a third-party analytics provider
milestones.description: Personal details of up to 250,000 customers, including names, identification numbers, emails, and IP addresses, were exposed through a global cyberattack on an external analytics service provider exploiting Metabase; customer funds and cryptocurrencies were not affected, and the incident was reported to the Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority. Paz froze Bitcoin purchases on its Yellow app in response.

name: Kerne USD
launchPhaseDetail: kUSD v2 is live on Base (first PSM mint 2026-05-14), but Pharos treats it as pre-active until a usable runtime price path exists. The protocol is in a genesis, capacity-capped phase: supply is about 1,135 kUSD (1,135.36 on Base, November 22 2026), DefiLlama stablecoin id 402 exposes supply with price=null, CoinGecko does not resolve a Kerne USD coin, and the v1 WETH/Hyperliquid hedge vault leg is disclosed-degraded and excluded from reserves so kUSD is currently 100% USDC-backed through three PSM reserves. Staking wrapper skUSD (ERC-4626, 0x96F5102C15b839757f811A98CEc3725Ac21DfA14) is deployed with a published live APY but near-zero third-party stake. The previous skUSD (0xdEd74F7E) is retired. kUSD role administration and all three PSMs' administration and manager configuration are behind a 48-hour TimelockController; the 2-of-3 Safe is its sole proposer, executor, and canceller, while a fixed PauseGuardian preserves immediate Safe-triggered PSM pausing. skUSD remains directly administered by the Safe, but its non-upgradeable wrapper powers do not confer kUSD minting or PSM control. Hourly signed proof of reserves is published at kerne.fi/verify. An ungoverned kUSD/USDC isolated market on Euler v2 (Base), deployed by Kerne on August 9 2026, carried no collateral or borrows at deployment.

milestones.title: First kUSD mint on Base through the Peg Stability Module
milestones.description: kUSD v2 minted 1:1 against USDC via the on-chain PSM on Base.

milestones.title: Independent researcher review published
milestones.description: Anonymized independent researcher review published at kerne.fi/security/audits; not a formal third-party audit.

milestones.title: Patched Peg Stability Module cutover completed; minting open on Base
milestones.description: The patched KUSDPSM completed cutover and is live with open 1:1 USDC minting (10 bps fee) in the protocol's Genesis Phase.

milestones.title: Hexens publishes final external audit report

milestones.title: kUSD and PSM administration completes 48-hour timelock transition
milestones.description: A 13-call operation scheduled on 2026-08-03 and executed on 2026-08-06 after 65 hours 32 minutes completed the handover: the TimelockController holds kUSD and PSM default-admin roles plus PSM manager roles, while the Safe's direct downstream roles were removed. The 2-of-3 Safe remains the timelock's sole proposer, executor, and canceller. A fixed PauseGuardian can only forward an immediate pause to the three PSMs.

milestones.title: Hexens audit report reissued: eight of ten KerneVault findings fixed in source, vault remains closed to deposits

milestones.title: Kerne deploys an ungoverned kUSD/USDC isolated market on Euler v2 (Base)
milestones.description: After a five-week forum review with no curator willing to open a market, Kerne deployed an Euler Edge market itself with a fixed 1:1 oracle and 60%/65% LTV. The market held zero collateral and zero borrows at posting.

name: RAI Dollar
launchPhaseDetail: Built by the Reflexer team as a successor to RAI, combining Liquity's redemption floor and Stability Pool with a RAI-style controller pinned to $1. Docs and the introductory post went live 2026-07-21 and describe a finished mainnet deployment configuration for seven collateral branches, but no contract addresses are published (the deployed-addresses registry and the RDToken FAQ entry both read TBD), the core repository is private, and the audits reference page states external security audits are in progress with audit-targeted commits still to be tagged. RAI Dollar was selected for the Ethereum Foundation Audit Subsidy Program on 2026-08-04, with the team describing the subsidy as funding independent audits ahead of a public testnet and launch. On 2026-10-21 the team announced a partnership with Pashov Audit Group to perform a security audit, which the site lists as underway. The same post named a targeted Q1 2027 launch, the basis for Pharos's expected launch date. The site states that a public Sepolia testnet is live; Pharos holds RD at auditing until audit reports or mainnet launch. In an October 26 2026 Rocket Pool GMC grant application, founder Bert Kellerman proposed a second security audit by Dedaub covering the protocol and rETH branch, targeting a January 5 2027 start while the Pashov audit is underway.

milestones.title: Public docs and blog post launch
milestones.description: Reflexer's team introduced RD as an immutable, $1-targeting CDP stablecoin on Ethereum with no governance, admin keys, or upgrade path, combining Liquity redemptions and Stability Pool with a RAI-style rate and par controller. Borrowers can opt a trove into Redemption Shield, paying a surcharge on the branch rate so that the trove is skipped by redemptions outside branch shutdown; unshielded troves on the same branch receive a rate discount, both set from the branch's shield share on one immutable curve. Bad debt left after a branch shutdown is repaid by routing three flows into the shut-down branch until the debt is cleared, with no vote or treasury: 50% of the MOAI-staker share of system-wide interest, the redemption fees from every healthy branch (normally retained), and a 0.5% bad-debt surcharge on redemptions; the team describes MOAI stakers as the protocol's risk capital and says Stability Pool and LP stakers are not diluted.

milestones.title: Selected for the Ethereum Foundation Audit Subsidy Program
milestones.description: The team said the subsidy will help fund independent security audits as it prepares for public testnet and launch. No audit reports have been published yet.

milestones.title: Pashov Audit Group engaged to audit RAI Dollar
milestones.description: RAI Dollar announced a partnership with Pashov Audit Group to perform a security audit of the immutable RAI Dollar lending protocol and said this brings it closer to its targeted Q1 2027 launch.

milestones.title: Founder seeks grant for a second audit by Dedaub
milestones.description: Founder Bert Kellerman's Rocket Pool GMC grant application proposes a second security audit by Dedaub covering the protocol and rETH branch, targeting a January 5 2027 start while the Pashov audit is underway.

name: Bank Consortium USD Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Announced September 1 2026 in a joint press release issued from London and New York: twenty-one financial institutions committed to establish a new jointly owned company in H2 2026, subject to closing conditions, to support the issuance of a stablecoin. The company name will be announced in due course. The group comprises Bank of America, Capital One, Citi, Fidelity Investments, Goldman Sachs, PNC Financial Services, Scotiabank, TD Bank Group, Wells Fargo, and WisdomTree (North America); Banco Santander, BBVA, Commerzbank, Credit Agricole, Deutsche Bank, Lloyds Banking Group, Cooperatieve Rabobank U.A., and UBS (Europe); MUFG Bank (East Asia); Sirius International Holding (Middle East); and Standard Bank (Africa). The initial focus is a USD-denominated stablecoin, with a longer-term ambition to expand into additional G7 currencies and a EUR offering as a priority, and the group aims for its stablecoin solution to go to market in the first half of 2027. The initiative follows an October 2025 announcement in which an initial group of ten banks explored a 1:1 reserve-backed form of digital money on public blockchains, and it intends to be GENIUS Act and MiCA-compliant, as applicable. On November 10 2026 Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that the institutions had committed about $270 million to cover five years of operating costs for the venture, which the report calls Project Faro and expects to be incorporated in the United States. As of November 14 2026 neither the figure nor the name appears in the institutions' own announcements. No company name, ticker, chain, contracts, reserve composition, custodian, or attestation arrangement has been announced.

milestones.title: Twenty-one financial institutions commit to establish a joint stablecoin company; USD token targeted for market in H1 2027
milestones.description: Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, Santander, UBS, MUFG Bank and fourteen other institutions committed to establish a new company in H2 2026, subject to closing conditions, to support issuance of a stablecoin, with an initial focus on a USD-denominated offering, a EUR offering as the next priority, and market entry targeted for the first half of 2027. The initiative intends GENIUS Act and MiCA compliance, as applicable, and follows an October 2025 exploration by an initial group of ten banks.

name: USTX
launchPhaseDetail: tx launched USTX on October 20 2026, issued by Brale and backed 1:1 by US dollar reserves; users mint it on the tx chain by depositing USDC from Ethereum, Solana, Base or Polygon. The issuer has published no asset details, but the chain shows USTX, created on October 8 2026, as denom uustx-core1rfxrg75fzuq5hgnnymjgsxj70d9w9cs8xuza7x with 6 decimals, clawback enabled and an issuer-owned extension contract that can pause transfers and blacklist addresses. milestones.title: tx launches Brale-issued USTX

Users mint USTX on the tx chain by depositing USDC from Ethereum, Solana, Base or Polygon. No contract address, decimals or supply figure was published.

name: VersaBank VUSD
launchPhaseDetail: Internal USDVB pilot announced August 26, 2025, with limited designated external deposit-partner/client deployment planned. Pilot is not a supported catalog launch-phase enum, so no launchPhase is assigned. The bank had described commercial launch as subject to an OCC non-objection process, and its September 1, 2026 filing sought regulatory confirmation of deposit-insurance eligibility and the ability to pay interest. On October 1 2026 VersaBank said VersaBank USA is serving as issuer of Bank of North Dakota's Roughrider Coin, live on Fiserv's digital asset platform, with responsibility for minting, burning, custody and reserve asset management. On October 15 2026 VersaBank announced the US commercial phase, under which VersaBank USA is to issue VUSD, a tokenized deposit the release calls interest-paying and FDIC insurance-eligible. The release says the phase is in full compliance with U.S. federal banking regulations and cites recent certainty around the bank's compliance, but names no regulator decision, chain or date. Pharos tracks the commercial token as VUSD from October 15 2026; USDVB remains the pilot name. No current launch window or official chain-qualified asset addresses are established. Scope review, November 4 2026: Pharos retains VUSD as an in-scope pre-launch USD stable-value claim. VersaBank's October 15 release describes an interest-paying, FDIC insurance-eligible tokenized deposit and planned exchange listings, but publishes no chain, contract or launch date. Re-check permissioning and holder transferability once a chain or contract is published, before any promotion; promotion also requires the normal runtime price and positive supply gate.

milestones.description: The bank describes phased testing and limited external partner/client expansion before commercialization, with one USDVB per US$1 on deposit.

milestones.title: Alpen launches partner-integration Testnet III on Bitcoin Signet

milestones.title: Alpen announces USDC and CCTP for future mainnet

name: Japan Megabank JPY Stablecoin
launchPhaseDetail: Announced June 10 2026 by MUFG Bank, Mizuho Bank, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Japan's three largest banks, which entered a memorandum of understanding to establish a voluntary council for jointly examining operational frameworks, governance, and related matters toward a jointly issued stablecoin. The Three Banks aim to conduct actual commercial transactions during fiscal year 2026 (ending March 2027) using a stablecoin issued pursuant to a trust agreement under which they act as joint settlors and a trust bank or similar institution acts as trustee; the production trustee is not yet named. The council examines issuance infrastructure, system and scheme design, and governance, and will consider collaboration with other financial institutions that may participate in the future. The initiative builds on a demonstration experiment selected in November 2025 as a supported project under the Financial Services Agency's FinTech Proof-of-Concept Hub, part of the joint exploration the three banks have conducted since 2024 under the Project Pax lineage. Nikkei reporting on June 9 2026 described a yen-denominated token issued on MUFG's Progmat platform with a US dollar version to follow and a one trillion yen business-to-business volume target by 2028; the banks' own release names neither denomination nor platform. On October 16 2026 the banks reported a July 17 to 23 trial of the jointly issued model with Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking as trustee, trust assets held in bank deposits, no issuance cap, and circulation limited to bank-verified users; the release calls the design provisional. No ticker, production chain, production trustee, reserve composition, or attestation arrangement has been announced.

milestones.title: Three-bank stablecoin demonstration experiment selected for the FSA FinTech Proof-of-Concept Hub
milestones.description: The joint release records that the Three Banks had been jointly holding discussions aimed at issuance of the stablecoin through a demonstration experiment selected in November 2025 as a supported project under the Financial Services Agency's FinTech Proof-of-Concept Hub.

milestones.title: MUFG, Mizuho, and SMBC sign MOU for a jointly issued stablecoin with live transactions targeted in FY2026
milestones.description: Japan's three largest banks entered a memorandum of understanding to establish a voluntary council for jointly examining operational frameworks, governance, and related matters, and aim to conduct actual commercial transactions during fiscal year 2026 using a stablecoin issued pursuant to a trust agreement with the banks as joint settlors and a trust bank or similar institution as trustee.

The release frames the design as provisional and announces no production issuance date.

name: JPYdf
launchPhaseDetail: JPY DeFi launched on Ethereum mainnet on October 15 2026, so JPYdf is live. Pharos tracks it pre-launch only because no runtime price source admits it: on launch day DefiLlama and CoinGecko listed neither the token nor the protocol, and the DefiLlama contract-price endpoint returned no quote. The token is 0xb122f4a154f84708407213d6a715181180012f45 (18 decimals, Ethereum only, no registered bridge minter). At block 26196851 (08:54 UTC on October 15), supply was 91,738,933 JPYdf, about $581,000 at that day's yen rate, with 69.4 million borrowed against USDC and 22.3 million against wstETH. Trading was confined to one Uniswap v4 JPYdf/USDC pool created that morning with about $552,000 of liquidity. The token and the Liquity v2 core are non-upgradeable and the token owner is renounced. The dToken vault and strategy layer is upgradeable and pausable, and governance can recognize collateral losses, replace oracle sources after a 12-hour timelock and resume paused branches without delay. The governance, operator and guardian Safes are each 2-of-3 with the same three signers, although the documentation describes a higher quorum for loss recognition. The deployed JPY/USD staleness threshold is 30 hours, while the documentation describes 72 hours. Chain Defenders and Guardian reviewed the JPYdf-specific code. The docs list a Guardian Defender bounty contest with a submission period from October 14 to November 13 2026, and GitHub private vulnerability reporting for the SDK. JPYdf Foundation DAO LLC operates the app, which excludes Japanese residents, and does not disclose its domicile.

milestones.description: Public launch with wstETH and USDC branches. Supply reached 91.7 million JPYdf by 08:54 UTC, with no DefiLlama or CoinGecko listing.

name: dotUSD
launchPhaseDetail: Polkadot OpenGov referendum 1944 created dotUSD as Asset Hub asset 7873, with 6 decimals, and took effect on October 8 2026. Its first phase allows only capped one-to-one minting and redemption against USDT through a peg stability module, alongside a Treasury-funded DOT/dotUSD pool. DOT-collateral vaults are left to a later phase. On October 26 the Technical Fellowship disclosed an XCM bug that had removed about 4.06 million dotUSD from the recorded supply while the tokens stayed in the pool, and arbitrage against the imbalance cost the Treasury's liquidity position an estimated $1.3 million. Referendum 1961 restored the recorded supply on October 30 without changing any balance. Asset Hub showed 4,212,640.59 dotUSD across 60 accounts on November 1 2026. Pharos tracks dotUSD pre-launch because no admitted source prices it: CoinGecko's dotusd preview has a null price and DefiLlama has no listing. In Parity's November 2 2026 incident review, bkchr estimated the Treasury loss at about $1.381 million in DOT and described dotUSD as fully backed, with no account balance changes.

milestones.title: dotUSD proposal submitted to Polkadot OpenGov as referendum 1944
milestones.description: The Polkadot Community Foundation put forward the community-drafted dotUSD referendum, which asks the Treasury to seed the DOT/dotUSD pool with $2.5 million of USDT used to mint dotUSD and $2.5 million of DOT. Its first phase allows only capped one-to-one minting against USDT through a peg stability module, leaving DOT-collateral vaults to a later phase. The referendum was confirmed on October 7 and executed on October 8 2026.

milestones.title: dotUSD launches on Asset Hub
milestones.description: Referendum 1944 took effect, enabling the USDT peg stability module and a treasury-seeded DOT/dotUSD pool. DOT-collateral vaults remain a later phase.

milestones.title: XCM bug removes about 4.06 million dotUSD from recorded supply
milestones.description: The Polkadot Technical Fellowship disclosed that an XCM bug on Asset Hub had removed about 4.06 million dotUSD from the recorded token supply while the tokens remained in the DOT/dotUSD liquidity pool. Arbitrage against the resulting price imbalance cut the Treasury's liquidity position by an estimated $1.3 million. The Fellowship said it had fixed the bug through a whitelisted caller referendum and moved the impacted assets to a controlled account, and that user wallets and funds were unaffected.

milestones.title: Referendum 1961 restores dotUSD's recorded supply and unblocks Snowbridge
milestones.description: OpenGov referendum 1961, submitted on October 27 2026, executed on October 30. The runtime upgrade recalculated dotUSD's recorded supply from existing balances without changing any holder's balance, and restored the Bridge Hub weights whose change had put Snowbridge on hold.

milestones.title: Parity publishes its dotUSD incident review
milestones.description: Parity's bkchr estimated the Treasury loss at about $1.381 million in DOT and described dotUSD as fully backed, with no changes to account balances.

name: ZelleUSD
launchPhaseDetail: ZLUSD is live on Solana. Pharos tracks it pre-launch because no admissible source prices it. Early Warning Services, the operator of the Zelle network, unveiled ZelleUSD (ZLUSD) on June 11 2026 as its proprietary U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin and said it will support future international payments in other markets, alongside a Zelle remittance corridor to India expected before the end of 2026. The release named no issuer, chain or launch date. The issuer is Anchorage Digital Bank N.A.: the Solana Token-2022 mint 7NNkMtGACBbwJdMRYD2KchTKm2xBwnsb4bT7YSfRUWZ4 (6 decimals) was created on June 10 2026 with metadata on Anchorage's static host, and all 30 of its mint transactions were signed by C2QJ4HKLWzWRNprAmKoyd6YqXouVHFZuLKujdqtF4ZDt, the mint authority of the Anchorage-issued USDPT and USDGO mints that Western Union and OSL publish. The first tokens were minted on June 18 2026 under the placeholder name USDXDEV. On July 10 the metadata was renamed ZLUSD and now states that ZLUSD is issued for Zelle by Anchorage Digital Bank NA and is redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars. Ledger Insights reported on June 12 that the stablecoin was live and that Zelle app support would follow by the end of the year. No transfer-hook program is set and new token accounts open unfrozen, so transfers are not allowlisted. Holders have transferred tokens between wallets, and the freeze authority has frozen the accounts of five specific wallets. Anchorage's covered stablecoin terms limit issuance and redemption to ADB clients but allow on-chain transfers to other addresses, barring transfers that violate sanctions or other law. At slot 464063902 on November 1 2026, supply was 137,650.11 ZLUSD across 14 funded wallets, after 158,262.11 minted and 20,612 burned. At slot 472506602 on November 22 2026, supply was 147,651.11 ZLUSD. CoinGecko's zelleusd entry is a preview listing for this mint with no price or market cap, DefiLlama does not list ZLUSD, and no DEX pool exists for the mint.

milestones.title: Early Warning unveils ZelleUSD alongside a Zelle corridor to India
milestones.description: Early Warning Services, operator of the Zelle network, unveiled ZelleUSD (ZLUSD) as its proprietary U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin to support future international payments in other markets. It also named India as the first country where U.S. consumers can send money abroad with Zelle, with initial availability expected before the end of 2026. The release named no issuer, chain or launch date for ZLUSD.

milestones.title: Anchorage Digital Bank mints the first ZLUSD on Solana
milestones.description: Mint authority C2QJ4HKLWzWRNprAmKoyd6YqXouVHFZuLKujdqtF4ZDt, which also mints the Anchorage-issued USDPT and USDGO, minted 1.33 tokens on mint 7NNkMtGACBbwJdMRYD2KchTKm2xBwnsb4bT7YSfRUWZ4. The mint had been created on June 10 under the placeholder name USDXDEV, and these tokens remain part of ZLUSD supply.

milestones.title: Solana mint renamed ZLUSD with Anchorage-hosted issuer metadata
milestones.description: The token metadata changed from USDXDEV to ZLUSD and now points to Anchorage's static host, which describes ZLUSD as a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued for Zelle by Anchorage Digital Bank NA and redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars.

GateHub's November 5 announcement says EURGH is available through its XRP Ledger and Xahau wallets, with issuance against received euros and at-par redemption through SEPA, subject to legal and verification requirements. milestones.description: GateHub announces the euro e-money token issued by Dinaro on XRP Ledger and Xahau. The release identifies the issuer account and currency code, describes funding through SEPA and gives holders at-par redemption rights subject to legal and verification requirements.

name: RDUSD
launchPhaseDetail: Anchorage Digital announced that Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. will issue RDUSD, with each token backed 1:1 by US dollars held at the bank. Anchorage will manage issuance, reserves, minting, redemption and custody. RD Technologies supports brand development and the application ecosystem, and deployment is planned on HSK Chain. RD Technologies' November 1 release and its November 2 website publication restrict Hong Kong distribution to professional investors and state that RDUSD is not licensed by the HKMA or approved or recognised by any Hong Kong regulatory authority. milestones.title: Anchorage Digital announces RDUSD with RD Technologies
milestones.description: Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. will issue the US dollar stablecoin and manage its reserves and redemption, while RD Technologies supports brand development and its application ecosystem. The announcement plans deployment on HSK Chain without setting a launch date.

milestones.title: HashKey On-Chain partners with RD Technologies to support RDUSD testing on HSK Chain
milestones.description: HashKey On-Chain announced a partnership with RD Technologies centred on RDUSD, covering on-chain trading, settlement, treasury management and asset tokenization. name: CHF-S
launchPhaseDetail: Safirum AG of Canton Zug announced CHF-S on June 22 2026 as a Swiss franc stablecoin on Solana's Token-2022 standard, with wallet-level KYC whitelisting built into the token and a launch planned for the third quarter of 2026. Safirum launched CHF-S on November 3 2026, and Maverix Securities says it was the first company to mint it. Safirum states that the token is fully backed by Swiss francs held in segregated accounts at Swiss-based banks, that every user must pass identity verification, and that CHF-S can only be transferred between approved wallets. Transfers carry a fee of 0.05% of the amount, capped at 0.50 CHF-S, plus network fees. Safirum is a member of the VQF, a self-regulatory organisation recognised by FINMA, and its launch release cites FINMA Supervisory Notice 06/2024 as a design requirement. Its releases do not name the reserve banks, and Safirum has published no mint address, supply figure or reserve attestation. Pharos keeps CHF-S pre-launch because neither a price lane nor a supply lane has been admitted.

milestones.title: Safirum announces CHF-S, a Swiss franc stablecoin on Solana
milestones.description: Safirum AG announced CHF-S on Solana's Token-2022 standard, backed by Swiss franc reserves in segregated accounts at Swiss custodian banks, with wallet-level KYC whitelisting built into the token and a launch planned for the third quarter of 2026.

milestones.title: CHF-S launches on Solana
milestones.description: Safirum announced that CHF-S had launched that day, fully backed by Swiss francs held at Swiss-based banks and transferable only between approved wallets after identity verification. Maverix Securities says it was the first company to mint CHF-S. The release gives no mint address, supply figure or attestation.

name: AllUnity SEKAU
launchPhaseDetail: AllUnity launched SEKAU on June 19 2026 with institutional minting and redemption and public-chain transfers. Its product page now advertises Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Solana, Tempo and Arc. Pinned reads on November 15 2026 verified six decimals and 11.23 SEKAU on Base at block 57973837, with zero token stock on Ethereum at block 26423673 and Polygon at block 97386379. These are deployment token stocks, not an admitted whole-asset circulating supply. The issuer-linked Solana address is an executable program, not a token mint, at finalized slot 469913062; no Solana supply or token decimals were established. Tempo and Arc RPC reads were unavailable, so their decimals and supply remain unverified. Only the three independently verified EVM token deployments are recorded here. The issuer's public-chain launch and positive Base issuance support launched status, while price and whole-asset supply remain unavailable to Pharos. Pharos tracks the SEK peg as OTHER until Swedish krona peg support is built.
